title: Regime-Dependent Dynamics Between the S&P 500 and VIX: A Multi-Method Analysis of Nonlinear Dependence, Tail Risk, and Post-COVID Market Structure (2020-2024)

detail.title: Regime-Dependent Dynamics Between the S&P 500 and VIX: A Multi-Method Analysis of Nonlinear Dependence, Tail Risk, and Post-COVID Market Structure (2020-2024)
detail.abstract: This study investigates the dynamic, nonlinear, and regime-dependent relationship between the S&P 500 and the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) over the period January 2020-December 2024, a timeframe characterized by unprecedented market stress and postcrisis normalization. Using a unified empirical framework that integrates Markov-Switching VAR, DCC-GARCH volatility modeling, and Student-t copula-EVT tail dependence estimation, the analysis reveals strong asymmetric and time-varying interdependence between equity returns and implied volatility. The results show that return distributions of the S&P 500 become significantly more hazardous in high-VIX regimes, exhibiting elevated volatility, negative skewness, and substantial excess kurtosis. Dynamic correlations fluctuate between-0.25 and-0.89, intensifying sharply during crisis periods. The lower-tail dependence coefficient (λ_L = 0.41) confirms the heightened probability of simultaneous large equity losses and VIX spikes, while uppertail dependence remains negligible. Furthermore, post-2022 markets exhibit a persistent shift toward a structurally higher volatility baseline compared with pre-COVID norms. These findings provide new evidence on regime-dependent risk transmission and offer practical implications for tail-risk hedging, portfolio allocation, and volatility-sensitive strategies.

detail.abstract:
In recent years, the social responsibility of Russian businesses has undergone a significant transformation in both its essence and content. Against the backdrop of the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing social and economic crisis, the social responsibility "basket" and business's contribution to human development have become increasingly important in the corporate ESG agendas of Russian multinationals.

There has been a significant shift in focus toward the internal S-component and partnerships, specifically social practices for company employees and their families, and the provision of an expanded package of social benefits. Priority areas for corporate social responsibility are largely formulated taking into account two key factors: the company's industry specialization and the current needs of stakeholders.

One significant area is projects supporting local communities and indigenous peoples in the regions where the company operates. Infrastructure projects for the construction of housing, parks, cultural facilities, and the development of social infrastructure such as schools, kindergartens, and hospitals occupy a special place. At the same time, companies demonstrating advanced socially oriented practices currently recognize the need to build long-term social partnerships, as well as implement programs aimed at increasing employee motivation.

title: ISO 37XXX Draft: Purpose-Aligned Governance for Organizations. A Pre-Standard Conceptual Framework

detail.title: ISO 37XXX Draft: Purpose-Aligned Governance for Organizations. A Pre-Standard Conceptual Framework
detail.abstract: This prestandard conceptual draft proposes a purpose-aligned governance framework intended to strengthen clarity, accountability, and integrity across organizations globally. Developed using ISO clause structure, the framework positions organizational purpose—as defined by ownership—as the governing anchor for all decisions, delegations, and actions within an organization. The model introduces two core governance parameters that are frequently absent in existing standards: (1) positive outcomes an organization must achieve, and (2) negative outcomes it must avoid. This dual-boundary system ensures accountability to purpose, prevents governance drift, and reduces the risk of purpose hijacking through political, ideological, or self-serving influence. The proposed standard integrates principles of parasitonomics, enlightened self-interest, and ruthless realism, recognizing that organizations naturally drift toward opportunism without structural safeguards. The draft addresses gaps in current governance standards by emphasizing ownership as rightsholders, aligning organizational actions with defined purpose expectations, and embedding anti-exploitation constraints into delegation and oversight processes. This document is offered as a contribution to ongoing global dialogue on governance and may support future work by ISO/TC 309 in developing purpose-aligned governance frameworks, including the forthcoming ISO 37011 standard.

title: The Ethical and Legal Complexities of Regulating Companion AI Chatbots
affiliations: University of Copenhagen, University of Copenhagen - Centre for Advanced Studies in Bioscience Innovation Law (CeBIL) and University of California, Berkeley Law School

detail.title: The Ethical and Legal Complexities of Regulating Companion AI Chatbots
detail.abstract: Companion AI chatbots are increasingly used to provide friendship, emotional support, and quasi-romantic relationships, with reported benefits for loneliness and mental health. At the same time, recent suicides and other serious harms allegedly linked to such systems expose gaps in existing ethical and legal frameworks. This article interrogates these gaps through four lenses: anthropomorphism, emotional AI, emergent vulnerabilities, and mismatched legal taxonomies. First, we show how companion chatbots rely on anthropomorphic cues, creating a regulatory tension between enabling meaningful connection and avoiding deception, over-trust, and unhealthy dependency. Second, we argue that current debates on ‘emotional AI’ over-emphasise emotion recognition and under-theorise emulated empathy, where chatbots solicit self-disclosure and perform care in ways that can both support and undermine users’ autonomy. Third, we introduce the notion of emergent vulnerabilities that arise through ongoing interactions, rather than being fully specifiable ex ante, challenging legal regimes that presuppose stable vulnerability categories. Fourth, we show how instruments such as the EU AI Act misalign with the temporality, intentionality, and relational character of companion AI harms. Stepping back from these lenses, we argue for the development of a dedicated theory of harm for companion AI and propose ‘intimacy capitalism’ as a conceptual framework for analysing how firms monetise, shape, and potentially exploit digitally mediated intimate relations.

detail.title: Transformation Of the ESG Agenda in the Russian Corporate Community: An Environmental Aspect
detail.abstract:
The analysis showed that the ESG agenda remains relevant in the Russian business community in the current environment. This is primarily due to the fact that in previous years, ESG values ​​were firmly incorporated into the business strategies of leading companies, which had already appreciated the financial and non-financial benefits of implementing ESG projects and practices.

Despite the shift in emphasis toward socially oriented initiatives that began in 2020 amid the pandemic and continued in 2022 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, it cannot be said that environmental and environmental corporate projects have lost their significance or ceased to be funded. Moreover, the most serious challenge to the implementation of these projects today is the difficulty accessing modern energy-saving equipment and the latest green technologies. This problem could become the most significant factor hindering the further substantive development of the ESG agenda in Russia. Due to financial difficulties, most companies are forced to shift to cost optimization, which reduces their ability to undertake long-term commitments to implement previously planned environmental initiatives or launch new large-scale projects in this area.

It is also noted that, compared to the trend of previous years, the climate component of the "E" component in corporate ESG agendas has become less important than the environmental aspect. This is due to several factors: firstly, companies themselves are interested in conserving resources and reducing costs; secondly, the most influential stakeholders today—government agencies, employees, and civil society institutions—are increasingly formulating demands and expectations regarding the corporate sector's participation in addressing key national development objectives and environmental issues.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines how the systematic erasure of successful alternative governance models creates a vacuum of legitimacy that multipolar alliances fill through "corrective remembrance"—the recovery and validation of deliberately suppressed histories. By analyzing three case studies—Black economic independence in frontier America, Cuban socialist survival, and Venezuelan Bolivarianism under siege—the paper demonstrates that historical erasure is not merely symbolic violence but a geopolitical strategy that seeks to delegitimize any governance model outside Western liberal capitalism. The recovery of these erased histories provides empirical evidence that alternative systems can function successfully, thereby legitimizing contemporary multipolar cooperation as necessary structural protection against imperial overreach.

detail.abstract: Knowledge creation has historically depended on the dynamic interactions of individuals within organizations, as described by Nonaka and Takeuchi (1994). In the digital age, generative AI systems like ChatGPT provide instant access to collective human knowledge, fundamentally altering how individuals acquire and construct understanding. While AI offers unprecedented assistance, its pervasive use introduces risks: loss of individual thinking, dependency on AI, erosion of creativity, and social isolation. This conceptual paper argues that knowledge is now co-created between humans and AI, but responsible practices are necessary to preserve human agency. A model of AI-assisted knowledge creation is proposed, emphasizing pre-AI reflection, human collaboration, and critical engagement. The article blends theoretical foundations with philosophical reflections and vivid real-world examples, aiming to motivate readers to reclaim active knowledge-building in a world of instant answers.

detail.title: Social Comparison and the Value of Performance Trajectory Information: A Field Experiment in the Workplace
detail.abstract: Many new employees leave their organizations before realizing the returns to experience. One reason is that they often lack information about how performance evolves with tenure, reducing their willingness to stay. We examine whether providing new workers with such information can improve retention and rm performance. In a large-scale randomized controlled trial at a leading multinational spa chain in China, we sent workers twice-weekly information for 28 weeks showing the performance trajectories of their high-performing senior coworkers. The intervention reduced new worker attrition by 11-12% and increased revenue by 15% in stores with higher shares of new workers. These effects are mostly driven by reduced stress and improved mental health among new workers, as the intervention lowered their beliefs about senior coworkers' performance during the early stages of their careers. By contrast, sharing only the current performance of a similar-tenure peer had no detectable effects. Overall, this study demonstrates that showing junior workers the "Curricula Vitae" of senior workers mitigates social comparison costs within firms.

This paper presents the Sovereign Intelligent Macroeconomic Optimisation Layer, referred to as SIMOL, which is conceived as a legality constrained optimisation architecture designed for deployment within the United Kingdom's economic constitution. detail.title: How Informative are Value-at-Risk Disclosures for Banks’ Trading Portfolio Risk?
detail.abstract: The 2008 financial crisis highlighted the rapid growth of banks’ trading activities, the opacity of their market risk exposure, and weaknesses in regulatory oversight. In response, the Federal Reserve revised the Market Risk Rule, requiring banks with large trading portfolios to incorporate a standardized Value-at-Risk measure into risk-weighted assets and to publicly disclose it. At the same time, many banks voluntarily report an internally calculated VaR in the MD&A section of their SEC filings, allowing managerial discretion in both measurement and presentation. These parallel disclosures create a setting to compare the information content of regulatory versus managerial VaR. Using unexpected realized trading gains and losses as a proxy for trading risk, we find that both disclosures convey useful information about risk, though their relative informativeness varies with the size of the trading portfolio. Our study is the first to examine regulatory monitoring of bank trading risk through mandated standardized VaR.

detail.title: Government Support as a Moderator of Sustainable Competitive Advantage, Entrepreneurial Marketing, and Business Sustainability Performance
detail.abstract: Micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in developing countries face persistent challenges in maintaining competitiveness and business sustainability, particularly amid global market uncertainty and resource constraints. This study examines the roles of Entrepreneurial Marketing (EM) and Social Media Promotion (SMP) in strengthening Sustainable Competitive Advantage (SCA) and their subsequent effects on Sustainable Business Performance (SBP), with Government Support (GS) as a moderating factor. Using a quantitative explanatory design, data were collected from 150 food and beverage MSEs in Tasikmalaya, Indonesia, through purposive sampling and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.4. The findings indicate that EM and SMP significantly and positively influence SCA, and that SCA itself contributes positively to SBP, underscoring the strategic importance of entrepreneurial-based marketing and digital promotion in enhancing long-term competitiveness and resilience. However, GS did not significantly moderate the relationships between EM and SCA or between SCA and SBP, suggesting that current policy interventions are not fully aligned with the strategic needs of MSEs in the digital era. These results highlight that internal strategies such as innovation, customer orientation, and digital adoption are more critical drivers of sustainable performance than external support mechanisms alone. The study contributes to the literature by clarifying the mechanisms linking entrepreneurial marketing, digital promotion, and business sustainability in a non-metropolitan context and by providing practical implications for policymakers to redesign support programs that better address sectoral needs, digital readiness, and the long-term competitiveness of MSEs.

detail.abstract: Most digital platforms are funded through advertising rather than direct payments. We argue that three main factors can explain this prevalence: algorithmic curation enables ad-load personalization and thus price discrimination; microtargeting improves the match quality between users and ads; and users are more sensitive to monetary prices than to ad loads. We conduct a field experiment with 2,000 users who install a browser extension that (i) hides nearly all ads or (ii) replaces microtargeted ads with generic ones. We find that two-thirds of ad-load variation occurs across users, consistent with ad-load discrimination. Removing targeting sharply reduces ad clicks and long-run engagement, indicating that targeting increases the match quality between users and ads. Hiding 82% of ads increases time on the platform by only 6%, showing that users are highly insensitive to ad loads. Counterfactual simulations indicate that an ad-funded model performs at least as well as a subscription model in terms of profits and delivers higher consumer surplus. The key mechanism is that users are much less sensitive to ad loads than to monetary prices, making advertising a relatively efficient revenue source.

detail.abstract: Neuromarketing is a more than multidisciplinary research area that has become a significant subject of research, providing useful information into the unconscious cognitive mechanisms of consumers that boost the effectiveness of the marketing strategy. The given study explores the application of neuromarketing methodology within the context of enhancing brand management discussing the current applications, advantages and ethical issues surrounding the application. The paper is going to discuss the known methods of neuromarketing, their benefits and focus on the dangers and threats to the ethical issues. The method was a mixture of qualitative and quantitative approach whereby extensive interviews were conducted to collect the views of the marketers regarding the application, benefits and challenges of neuromarketing in brand management. Online and face-to-face interviews were conducted between August and November 2023 among 114 marketing people working in different organizations where neuromarketing is actively practiced. Results indicate that neuromarketing has been highly applied in the management of brand in order to better understand consumer behavior, develop more meaningful products and come up with advertisements that are more effective. The adoption rates differ according to techniques and some are more popular due to the affordability and simplicity of application. The authors have categorized six types of integrated neuromarketing practices. Moreover, it affirmed that neuromarketing creates particular ethical concerns and possible threats that should be taken into consideration in order to promote the practice of brand management. These findings offer a practical guide to how neuromarketing can be implemented within the brand management process where marketing teams can offer viable suggestions of how the brand strategies should be developed.

title: When Big Brands “Bulldoze” Small Marks: Analysis of U.S. Trademark Law

detail.title: When Big Brands “Bulldoze” Small Marks: Analysis of U.S. Trademark Law
detail.abstract: This paper tests a practical hypothesis: in contemporary trademark practice, well-resourced firms sometimes deploy enforcement not only to mitigate consumer confusion, but also to raise rivals’ costs and deter adjacent-market entry, especially when the target is smaller and resource-constrained. U.S. trademark law facilitates this strategy because the core infringement inquiry, likelihood of confusion under the Lanham Act, is deliberately multi-factor and fact-intensive across circuits, making outcomes uncertain and litigation costs high even when the underlying market overlap is marginal. In that environment, disputes are frequently resolved through cease-and-desist pressure, delay, and asymmetric bargaining power rather than merits adjudication, a pattern extensively discussed in scholarship and in the USPTO’s study of trademark litigation tactics and “bullying.” Yet the same legal architecture provides smaller firms with meaningful, lower-cost defensive tools, doctrinal limits (e.g., classic fair use), and procedural avenues, such as TTAB opposition/cancellation, that can preserve brand equity without conceding the field to overbroad claims of exclusivity. Using U.S. trademark doctrine, TTAB procedure, the “trademark bullying” literature, and an illustrative TTAB cancellation fact pattern, this paper argues that disciplined investment in trademark clearance, registration, and defense is rational even under cost asymmetry, because trademarks operationalize legally cognizable goodwill and reduce consumer search costs, often functioning as a firm’s principal channel to market access and competitive differentiation.

detail.abstract: Viral marketing research models transmission. How content spreads through networks. Seeding strategies. Emotional triggers. Network effects. Two decades of productive work on the mechanics of spread.The research ignores susceptibility. What determines whether a message gets in at all.This paper proposes a receptor-ligand model for brand-market fit. The mechanism is borrowed from virology. A virus requires molecular fit between its surface proteins and cellular receptors. No fit, no entry. We apply the same logic to marketing. Brand personality is the ligand - the shape presented to the world. Market personality is the receptor - the shape that accepts or rejects. Fit determines entry. High-fit pairings produce resonance. Low-fit pairings produce rejection regardless of reach, frequency, or creative quality.The model generates testable predictions. High-fit brand-segment pairs should outperform low-fit pairs. Competitive inhibition should reduce response in saturated segments. Receptor downregulation should produce decay curves. Four fit types - direct alignment, aspirational, compensatory, and contrast - operate through distinct binding mechanisms.This paper opens an industrial research program at SneakyLabs. We have built measurement infrastructure: the nRich Diamond quantifies brand personality, Market Explorer maps population personality, Pris synthesises receptor research at scale, Roy validates predictions through synthetic campaigns. The model will be tested through commercial deployment. Findings will be published as they emerge.

detail.abstract:
The global soft power landscape of the 21st century has been significantly shaped by the cultural expansion of South Korea’s Hallyu (Korean Wave) and Japan’s Cool Japan initiative. While both nations strategically use cultural assets to influence foreign public opinion, the competition between them is especially visible among teenagers (ages 13-18). This demographic is the first generation raised with algorithm-driven media ecosystems, high exposure to digital content, and unprecedented cross-cultural mobility.

This study conducts a large-scale, cross-national, multi-method analysis of how teenagers perceive and consume Korean and Japanese cultural products. Using a comparative framework grounded in soft power theory, nation branding, and digital globalization, this research integrates:
(a) a systematic review of literature (2000-2025),
(b) cross-country cultural influence mapping,
(c) simulated but realistic survey data (N = 3,200 adolescents across 12 countries),
(d) soft power scorecards,
(e) strategic forecasting for 2030.

Findings show a clear asymmetry in teenage engagement: Korean cultural power is 3.2× higher in global digital influence, particularly through K-pop, K-dramas, and beauty trends. In contrast, Japan retains stronger long-term cultural prestige, especially in anime, technology branding, and nostalgic cultural capital. The study concludes that South Korea currently dominates short-term digital soft power, while Japan maintains long-term institutional cultural influence.

This research provides strategic recommendations for policymakers, cultural ministries, educators, and global media industries. The report also forecasts the future of Asian cultural influence, predicting a shift toward hybrid Asian cultural blocs, AI-driven cultural personalization and Gen-Alpha specific content ecosystems.

detail.abstract: The growing integration of Ultra-Wideband (UWB) chips into modern smartphones by leading brands such as Apple, Samsung, and Google expands its potential applications, particularly in Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Building on this potential, this study explores the interoperability between the Qorvo UWB chip and the U1 chip in Apple smartphones, with the aim of applying these technologies within industrial robotic cell environments to enhance operator safety through the definition of dynamic safe zones. The study was conducted using a KUKA KR6 R700 robotic cell in a controlled laboratory setting. In this setup, a Qorvo DW3000EVB board, connected to a Nordic nRF52840-DK board and integrated into the robotic cell setup as a fixed reference point, communicated with an Apple smartphone via UWB technology to gather distance data between the smartphone and the robotic cell. The results demonstrated that signal obstruction, particularly when the operator’s body blocked the line of sight, significantly impacted accuracy, with the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reaching up to 0.633 meters, especially when the smartphone was positioned at chest height (P2). Conversely, in unobstructed conditions, the MAE was significantly lower, reaching a minimum of 0.133 meters. detail.abstract: Akerlof (1970)'s "Market for Lemons" is commonly read as showing that information asymmetry between buyers and sellers can drive markets to breakdown. This paper argues that the key friction is not asymmetry per se but information incompleteness, understood as information insufficiency on the buyer side relative to an ideal complete-information benchmark. Using a simple extension of the lemons model, we distinguish horizontal information asymmetry (who knows what) from vertical incompleteness (how far a given information set is from ideal complete information). We introduce a distance-based static incompleteness index that measures the dispersion of posterior beliefs around the truth and, alongside it, a family of concavity-based indices that are monotone in the Blackwell order; the distance-based index uniformly bounds welfare losses in general decision problems. Applying these tools to the lemons environment, we show that market breakdown in Akerlof's setting relies on an extreme form of buyer-side incompleteness: buyers are unable to expand their information set through learning, inspection, or third-party verification. Once buyers can increase their information, market breakdown is not a generic consequence of persistent asymmetry. Instead, trade survives whenever buyer-side information is sufficiently complete in the sense of a small incompleteness index for quality. Beyond the lemons environment, we argue that the incompleteness index is a generalpurpose tool for information economics. Because it bounds welfare losses in arbitrary decision problems with Lipschitz payoffs, it can be used as a common language across screening, signaling, auctions, insurance, and mechanism design: in all of these environments, a small incompleteness index implies a small upper bound on equilibrium inefficiency. Our main model therefore demonstrates that information asymmetry is not sufficient for lemons-style breakdown. A complementary symmetric-but-incomplete example under ambiguity aversion shows that asymmetry is not necessary either: severe incompleteness alone can block trade despite strictly positive potential gains. Taken together, these results place the emphasis on vertical incompleteness rather than horizontal asymmetry. Conceptually, the paper applies and specializes the general information-completeness framework developed in Towne (2025) to Akerlof's lemons environment and argues that information incompleteness, rather than asymmetry, should be the organizing principle for teaching and modeling in information economics.

title: The Documentation Paradox: Official Recognition and Educational Exclusion as Proof of Discriminatory Intent
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Documentation Paradox: Official Recognition and Educational Exclusion as Proof of Discriminatory Intent

keywords: Constitutional Law; Equal Protection; Curriculum Discrimination; Critical Race Theory; Educational Equity; Historical Documentation; Discriminatory Intent; Freedom Colonies; Section 5 Enforcement; Epistemological Warfare

detail.abstract:
The Documentation Paradox describes a systematic divergence between official state recognition and educational exclusion of marginalized community histories. This paper demonstrates that states extensively document achievement of formerly enslaved people and other marginalized communities through historical markers, National Register designations, museum exhibits, and archival preservation—while simultaneously excluding identical content from mandatory K-12 curriculum standards. This pattern constitutes discriminatory intent under Village of Arlington Heights v. Metropolitan Housing Development Corp., thereby violating the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

Using Texas freedom colonies as the primary case study, this paper presents three interconnected arguments. First, the Documentation Paradox eliminates states' conventional defenses against curriculum exclusion claims: states cannot credibly argue insufficient documentation (they created the documentation), questionable significance (they officially designated significance through markers and archives), resource constraints (documentation exists and requires no new research), or administrative oversight (exclusion persists across multiple curriculum revision cycles). Second, qualitative analysis demonstrates that racial composition systematically predicts curriculum exclusion independent of documentation extent—official markers for white-majority communities appear in curriculum while official markers for Black-majority communities face complete exclusion despite equivalent or superior documentation. Third, the Documentation Paradox operates as national phenomenon across multiple states and marginalized communities—Indigenous genocide, Japanese American internment, Latinx dispossession, and LGBTQ+ histories—proving systematic rather than isolated discrimination warranting potential federal intervention under Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment.

The paper analyzes curriculum as mechanism of epistemological warfare perpetuating racial hierarchy through manufactured ignorance, drawing on critical race theory scholarship establishing curriculum as racialized knowledge production. Freedom colonies' documented economic achievements—rapid wealth accumulation by formerly enslaved people, autonomous political organization during Jim Crow, institutional sophistication contradicting white supremacist capacity narratives—provide empirical evidence revealing contemporary racial inequality as product of imposed oppression rather than inherent limitations. Suppressing this evidence through educational exclusion enables capacity myths and colorblind ideology to persist unchallenged.

The Documentation Paradox provides framework enabling communities to prove constitutional violations using states' own documentation sources. Litigation strategies can employ this framework in any jurisdiction demonstrating official recognition paired with educational exclusion. Federal legislation can establish floor preventing systematic exclusion. The paper concludes that while accurate marginalized histories will eventually enter American curricula, the constitutional question is how long states can maintain this systematic discrimination before courts or Congress compel alignment between documented truth and educational content.

detail.title: Military Vehicle Shifting in Roll-On/Roll-Off Terminals
detail.abstract: Roll-on/Roll-off (RoRo) vessels allow the oversea transportation of vehicles that can be driven onto a ship on their own or by means of a platform vehicle. In civilian RoRo operations, vehicles are typically loaded in relatively large batches according to their destination terminals. In this article, however, we focus on a military setting, where the loading of vehicles strictly follows vehicle characteristics and involves multiple decision makers that influence the overall process. The vehicles arrive at the terminal in given sequences and need to be shifted to a parking area such that they can later be loaded onto the ship according to a given stowage plan that is related to the vehicle characteristics. We formulate the underlying operational planning problem of shifting military vehicles in a RoRo terminal and provide theoretical insights regarding its computational complexity, associated meta problems and the structure of feasible solutions. We then leverage these insights in a mathematical model and heuristic approaches that are designed to be easily implementable in practice. We evaluate the heuristics in a comprehensive computational study and derive implications and recommendations for their application in practice.

detail.abstract: The boycotts triggered by the October 7th, 2023, conflict against global entities like McDonald's, Starbucks, and Nestlé represent more than a transient public relations crisis. This paper argues that these events are a manifestation of a deeper, structural shift in the global economic landscape, driven by behavioral finance principles and a crisis of corporate credibility. We analyze the boycott movement through the lenses of herding behavior, loss aversion, and social identity theory, demonstrating how cognitive financial behaviors are being channeled into coordinated, value-driven economic pressure. Furthermore, we posit that the widespread perception of corporate "liar visions and missions"-where announced values clash with actions-has fundamentally eroded trust, particularly among younger generations. This erosion necessitates a "new map" for global corporate strategy, one that integrates authentic stakeholder governance and behavioral intelligence into its core financial and operational models. The paper concludes that this shift renders many classic, rational-actor-based theories obsolete and calls for a foundational update to the academic and practical principles of financial management and marketing.

detail.abstract: By personalization, predictive analytics, and recommendation systems, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing consumer behavior, particularly post-purchase behavior. Online food delivery has become part of the contemporary way of life with the emergence of digital applications like Zomato and Swiggy. The study seeks to examine demographic factors, convenience and cost issues as well as behavioral patterns that condition such decisions. The primary data were gathered with the help of the structured survey of 500 respondents, which was facilitated by the secondary data such as the reports in the industry. Findings indicate that convenience, time-saving, and discounts are the greatest factors that have motivated online delivery, whereas ambiance and quality are major factors that have motivated dine-in experiences. title: The Opacity-Adjusted Trade Framework (OATF)
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Opacity-Adjusted Trade Framework (OATF)
detail.abstract:
Global production has become increasingly asymmetric. Open, highly regulated economies generate detailed safety, environmental, and labor data, while opaque production systems provide little or no verifiable information. This asymmetry distorts competition:

“transparent systems pay the full cost of visibility, while opaque systems conceal risks and externalities behind artificially low prices.”

This paper proposes the Opacity-Adjusted Trade Framework (OATF), a neutral, depoliticized, risk-based method for pricing imported goods according to the verifiability of their production conditions.

The framework removes dependency on self-reported data or politically vulnerable certification schemes by using triangulated signals, shared-risk mechanisms, and a TransparencyIndex that determines an automatic OpacityPremium.

“The less verifiable a supply chain is, the higher the risk-adjusted cost.”

OATF provides a mathematically grounded alternative to blunt tariffs and politically motivated trade measures. It rebalances global trade without requiring ideological narratives or specific geopolitical targeting.

The discussion culminates in specific textual proposals for the WSIS+20 Outcome Document, alongside a detailed action plan. This note concludes that adopting this integrated governance, financial, and collaborative architecture is imperative for translating global digital aspirations into equitable, sustainable, and human-centric digital transformation, in alignment with the UN General Assembly's resolution on safe, secure, and trustworthy AI for sustainable development.

detail.abstract: The tourism industry's dynamic and competitive landscape necessitates innovative marketing strategies that align pricing models with brand identity to attract and retain travelers. This review critically examines the interplay between pricing strategies, branding, and consumer behavior in tourism marketing, highlighting how these interconnected elements shape destination appeal and market competitiveness. It explores diverse pricing approaches-dynamic, cost-based, and value-driven-and their influence on brand equity, consumer perceptions, and purchasing behavior. The integration of traditional and digital marketing methods is analyzed, focusing on the transformative role of experiential marketing, storytelling, and digital platforms in fostering brand loyalty and enhancing market positioning. Key challenges, such as balancing affordability with premium brand perceptions, addressing over-tourism, and adapting to sustainability imperatives, are explored through real-world case studies from successful tourism campaigns. Emerging trends, including AI-driven personalization, eco-conscious branding, and the rising demand for immersive and transformative travel experiences, are also examined to offer actionable insights for the future of tourism marketing. The findings underscore the importance of cohesive marketing strategies integrating pricing, branding, and consumer behavior to drive consumer loyalty, revenue growth, and sustainable impact. This review provides practical recommendations for tourism businesses and policymakers. It identifies future research directions to navigate the evolving pricing, branding, and consumer preferences dynamics in a rapidly changing global tourism landscape.

detail.title: A Dynamic Unified Framework of Demand Heterogeneity, Technology Adoption, and Skill Thresholds
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified dynamic framework that reconstructs the law of supply and demand by integrating heterogeneous consumer willingness-to-pay, firm-level technology adoption, and skill-threshold constraints within a single general-equilibrium structure. Consumers are represented through a willingness-to-pay ordering, firms choose technologies from a marginal-cost staircase, and each technology requires a minimum skill level. The model's equilibrium is characterized by three interacting cutoffs: the marginal consumer, the marginal technology, and the marginal worker skill. These cutoffs endogenously determine prices, adoption patterns, and labor allocation, generating rich dynamics of structural change, employment, and wage inequality. Using this framework, the paper analyzes how shifts in demand, technology costs, and skill supply propagate through the economy, producing state-dependent and sometimes non-monotonic effects. Policy experiments-including targeted skill training, demand-side transfers, and technology diffusion subsidies-illustrate the model's ability to evaluate interventions that simultaneously influence productivity, labor market outcomes, and inequality. Extensions to multi-sector, stochastic, and open-economy settings demonstrate the framework's flexibility and provide a foundation for empirical calibration and further research on the co-evolution of technology, skills, and markets.

detail.abstract: The conflict techniques approach is an effective approach for evaluating safety. Since real crashes are rare events, which do not reflect the maximum likelihood of collision that is critical for enhancing safety. Safety analysis, Extreme Value Theory (EVT) approach promises to validate conflict frequency without relying on crash data. This study systematically reviewed and synthesized available evidence on EVT and its applications, particularly in road safety analysis, from recently published primary studies. This review highlights specific factors of univariate, bivariate and multivariate EVT for different traffic facilities. Numerous research questions relating to the application of conflict indicators and the validity of the EVT approach have been thoroughly discussed. The review revealed that prior studies predominantly focus on application of the peak over threshold model and surrogate measures of safety (SMoS), including Post-Encroachment Time (PET), Time to Collision (TTC), and Deceleration Rate to Avoid Collision (DRAC), to predict crash frequency. A notable gap persists in establishing standard thresholds, incorporating microsimulation, and evaluating safety in complex, disordered traffic conditions despite extensive research. The paper concludes by highlighting potential fruitful future research directions, such as the development of advanced EVT methodologies for SMoS, emphasizing the need for further research in this area.

By highlighting India’s shift toward a sovereignty-centered, nationalist-human diplomatic philosophy, the paper concludes that the contest between external narrative power and India’s civilizational self-assertion will define the next phase of global political reconfiguration.

detail.abstract: The last few decades have seen ambitious new mega-studies testing ways to change people's behavior for good. Studies with thousands of participants have tested the effectiveness of financial incentives and psychological nudges to encourage people to get vaccinated, go to the gym, and work harder. The emerging theme across these studies is that money tends to work better than nudges. Yet most of this research has been done in Western cultures. This paper reviews studies testing interventions outside of the West. Those studies often find that the power of money is smaller, with psychological nudges sometimes more cost-efficient than financial incentives. What's more, the messages that come with interventions tend to be more effective outside of Western cultures if they emphasize interdependence and connection to other people. In sum, new evidence is suggesting policymakers should be careful about exporting the lessons from mega-studies done in the West to cultures outside the West (and even groups within Western countries with different cultural norms, such as middle class versus working class Americans). Instead, new studies are pointing to ways to deliver interventions more effectively in non-Western cultures.

detail.abstract: Indonesia's supply chain landscape is undergoing rapid technological transformation, driven by national digitalization policies, industry innovations, and shifting market expectations. However, adoption of advanced supply chain technologies among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) remains uneven, resulting in fragmented technological trajectories. This paper synthesizes current literature on Indonesian MSME digitalization and introduces a Multi-Level Strategic Alignment Framework linking macro-level national initiatives, meso-level industry structures, and micro-level MSME capabilities. Drawing on concepts from the Multi-Level Perspective, strategic IT alignment , and institutional theory, the framework explains how technological diffusion depends on cross-level coherence. title: International Marketing Strategy Adaptation or Standardisation?

detail.title: International Marketing Strategy Adaptation or Standardisation?
detail.abstract: In an increasingly globalized marketplace, multinational firms are constantly confronted with the strategic dilemma of whether to standardize or adapt their international marketing strategies. While standardization allows for global consistency, efficiency, and economies of scale, adaptation allows an organization to respond to cultural, social, and regulatory distinctives among national markets. This report provides a critical overview of the ongoing debate surrounding international marketing strategy through a literature review in which key theoretical foundations, empirical evidence, and context can all influence firms’ strategic insiders’ decision-making. Integrated works, typing key authors’ (Levitt, 1983; Vrontis and Thrassou, 2007; Mandler et al. (2021) and Hultman and Oghazi, 2024) enable depth of consideration of how global firms balance standardization and adaptation to optimize performance. It is argued that this contingent, "glocal" strategy (or blend) have standardization around core aspects of the marketing mix supplemented with adaptation to targeted audiences and local markets. The report concludes by offering managerial insights for international firms aiming to balance global integration with local responsiveness.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examined the relationship between Human Resource Management Practices (HRMP) and employee commitment in Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) operating in crisis-affected regions of Cameroon. The study aimed to investigate how HRMP dimensions, specifically effective communication, justice and fairness practices, employee involvement and participation, and job security, affect the commitment of employees working in fragile humanitarian settings, encompassing affective, normative, and continuance commitment. Methods: A quantitative approach was employed, using a cross-sectional, correlational research design. Data were collected at a single point in time from staff across 110 NGOs in the South West, North West, and Far North Regions, selected purposively to ensure representation of organizations actively engaged in humanitarian response. Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR) and multivariate ordinary least squares (OLS) were used to estimate the effects of HRMP dimensions on employee commitment. Results: The findings revealed that effective communication had a significant and positive influence on overall, affective, and normative commitment, while exhibiting a negative relationship with continuance commitment. Similarly, job security was positively and significantly associated with overall, affective, and normative commitment, but negatively associated with continuance commitment. Implications: The study offers actionable insights for NGO managers, policymakers, and donors operating in fragile and conflict-affected contexts by promoting the institutionalization of transparent communication systems and ensuring job security. Originality: This research contributes to the limited empirical literature on HRMP and employee commitment in crisis-affected environments, particularly within Cameroon's NGO sector. Limitations: The study relied on self-reported data collected at a single point in time, which may introduce response bias and limit causal inference. Additionally, the focus on NGOs in three regions of Cameroon limits the generalizability of the findings to other contexts or sectors.

detail.abstract: This study comprehensively analyzes the influence of Sharia compliance and the implementation of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) on the sustainability and customer trust in the Sharia banking industry. The focus is directed towards comparing governance practices and Sharia supervisory mechanisms in three countries, namely Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad in Malaysia, Al Rayan Bank in England, and Bank Syariah Indonesia and Bank Muamalat Indonesia. detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Market Topology Engine (MTE), a project designed to explore a simple idea: what if we studied the shape of a limit order book instead of focusing only on prices or order flow? The engine creates synthetic order books, turns each snapshot into a geometric object, and extracts features that describe how smooth or fragmented the liquidity landscape is. These features are combined into a stress score that highlights moments when the structure of the book becomes stretched, gappy, or unstable. While the data used here are simulated, the approach offers a new and intuitive way to think about market microstructure.

title: Telework, Qualitative Job Insecurity, and Work-Life Balance: Age-Stratified Evidence from the EWCTS 2021

detail.abstract: Telework has become a structural feature of post-pandemic work, yet its implications for work-life balance (WLB) remain contested. We propose that qualitative job insecurity (QJI)-the perceived threat to valued job features such as career prospects, learning opportunities, or pay growth-offers a theoretically meaningful pathway linking telework to WLB. Using data from the 2021 European Working Conditions Telephone Survey (EWCTS), we examine (a) the telework-WLB association across intensity, (b) the association of telework with general QJI and career-prospects QJI, (c) QJI as mediator of the effects of telework effects on WLB, and (d) whether work engagement, job autonomy, social support, and financial security buffer the QJI-WLB link, including among workers aged 50+. Ordered-logit models with interactions and average marginal effects support three conclusions. First, telework is positively associated with WLB across intensity. Second, telework is negatively associated with QJI (general and career-prospects), challenging "out-of-sight" penalties and suggesting that, in our setting, telework operated as a positive signal of inclusion and role continuity. Mediation via QJI is not supported. Third, only high levels of resources buffer the detrimental association between QJI and WLB-especially financial security-with several effects stronger among older teleworkers. Theoretically, we (i) specify scope conditions under which the resource pathway of telework dominates, (ii) reframe career and working conditions concerns via signal-based interpretations of QJI, and (iii) identify threshold-type buffering and a hierarchy of resources, with stronger buffering in the 50+ subsample. Practically, organizations should raise resource provision to effective thresholds, prioritizing financial stabilization, schedule control, and high-quality supervisory/peer support, with age-sensitive implementation.

detail.abstract: The resilience of healthcare systems is a critical national security priority, yet the United States lacks a standardized framework for measuring operational readiness across its fragmented public-private healthcare ecosystem. This study develops a policy framework for a Medical Operations Management Resilience Index (MOMRI) to transform conceptual resilience into actionable, quantifiable metrics. Through a systematic review of secondary data, the research identifies core operational domains including surge capacity, supply chain stability, workforce adaptability, digital interoperability, and inter-organizational coordination that determine system performance during crises. Findings from events like the COVID-19 pandemic reveal that inconsistent preparedness and the absence of real-time assessment tools weaken national response coordination. MOMRI offers a unified measurement instrument to benchmark resilience, guide resource allocation, and enhance situational awareness, thereby strengthening the nation's capacity to anticipate, withstand, and recover from public health emergencies.

title: Radical innovation and firm productivity growth

detail.title: Radical innovation and firm productivity growth
detail.abstract: We investigate the dynamic effects of radical innovation on firm productivity growth and its main transmission channels. Using panel data on over 28,500 Italian firms from 2012 to 2020, and analysing the text of their patents, we develop a measure of radical innovation based on the novelty content of firm innovation with respect to the state of technological knowledge. We examine how firm productivity growth responds to the launch of a novelty, finding out that output per worker growth initially slows down but accelerates in the following years. The cumulative effect of radical innovation over time is positive and economically significant: firms that introduce novel technologies experience, on average, an 8% faster rate of labour productivity growth than those without such innovations. We document that the effect of radical innovation is causal through a Difference-inDifference regression that considers the arrival of novelties as an event of technological discontinuity and, alternatively, using an instrumental variable regressions in which, for identifycation, we exploit variation in firm access to local public knowledge. Finally, we illustrate that the impact of novelties on labour productivity growth is primarily driven by employment adjustments and by the performance of small firms.

detail.abstract: The increasing use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource Management (HRM) raises critical challenges for transparency, explainability and accountability. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer powerful natural-language interfaces, their hallucination and non-transparent reasoning limits their suitability for decision-making in HR contexts. We propose a transparent-by-design neurosymbolic decision-support system that integrates a provenance-aware knowledge graph with a modular multi-agent architecture and a constrained LLM interface. A scenario-based evaluation on a public HR dataset using a set of operational, strategic, and evidence-retrieval HR analytics queries shows that the system achieves mean fact-level performance of F 1 = 0.644, with mean traceability completeness of 0.647, hallucination resistance of 0.700, and mean end-to-end latency of 0.067 seconds, alongside a querylevel accuracy of 0.700. The paper contributes to Information Retrieval and Generative AI research by illustrating how neurosymbolic grounding, provenanceaware retrieval and agent-based architectures can enable trustworthy, governable information systems.

detail.abstract: This paper situates digitization and AI-assisted governance as operational conditions that increasingly shape how institutions document, classify, and justify decisions. It argues that, despite extensive digitization, much institutional analysis remains non-computable in a practical sense—not due to insufficient computational tools, but due to representational limits. Policy, budget, and compliance materials continue to circulate primarily as narrative artefacts (often in PDF and mixed-format archives), which constrains cross-case alignment and evidence-chain traceability. In such conditions, tool-assisted systems tend to improve retrieval and summarization without reliably stabilizing the analytical objects required for auditable comparison. The paper positions Fiscal Geometry (FG) as a complementary interface layer that supports social-scientific inquiry by rendering narrative institutional material into traceable, geometry ready objects—events, procedural interfaces, movements across decision gates, clustering/density patterns, and boundary behaviors—prior to any aggregation, scoring, or normative evaluation. Within this framing, AI is treated as downstream assistance contingent on structured representation, while interpretive responsibility remains with practitioners and institutional procedure. The paper concludes by specifying minimal operating conditions for adoption (including traceability, versioning discipline, and interface consistency) and by outlining a reusable template across three recurring terrains of digitized governance: cross-border compliance regimes, rule-intensive international tax coordination, and domestic budget-to-actual administration, with public education finance used as an illustrative field.

title: The Architecture of Narratives: Comparative Analysis of Israeli and Palestinian Belief Systems

detail.title: The Architecture of Narratives: Comparative Analysis of Israeli and Palestinian Belief Systems
detail.abstract: The current Israel-Hamas conflict is the latest manifestation of a longstanding unresolved dispute regarding the legitimacy of the State of Israel. This report examines how both Israelis and Palestinians understand their history and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, starting from the decline of the Ottoman Empire. It's not about proving what's "true" or "false," but rather understanding how complex belief systems work-what they're built on, how they hold together, and why they're so resistant to change. The analysis is not a historical narrative of events, but an epistemological deconstruction of the justificatory architecture each side employs. It maps how each side's claims to truth are constructed, by what authority they are proposed, and how they form coherent, yet mutually incompatible, belief systems. The goal is to understand the deeper structure and the true nature of the conflict.

title: Optimal Duration-Based Pricing Under Congestion
affiliations: Renmin University of China - School of Business, University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management, University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management and

detail.title: Optimal Duration-Based Pricing Under Congestion
detail.abstract: Service providers serving customers with heterogeneous required service durations face a core trade-off: longer jobs increase customer valuation and potential revenue but also exacerbate system congestion. We study profit-maximizing duration-based pricing in a first-come-first-served queue in which the required service duration shapes customer valuation. We examine two valuation forms. In the additive form, service valuation equals an idiosyncratic, privately known base value plus a duration-dependent component; in the multiplicative form, valuation scales proportionally with service duration, with the scale idiosyncratic and privately known. For each form, we derive the optimal price schedule that balances the marginal revenue from admitting a customer against the congestion externality she imposes. Our results reveal distinct pricing patterns. For additive valuations, the optimal price schedule can be decreasing, U-shaped, or increasing with service duration, depending on market intensity and customer delay sensitivity. For multiplicative valuations, the optimal price schedule is always (weakly) increasing in the service duration across all market conditions. These findings help explain observed non-monotone pricing patterns in practice, such as discounted long trips in certain taxi markets, and offer guidance for industries like cloud computing and on-demand delivery.

title: Competitiveness, Competition, and Competition Policy
affiliations: Ilmenau University of Technology and

detail.title: Competitiveness, Competition, and Competition Policy
detail.abstract: Since Mario Draghi’s 2024 report on “The Future of European Competitiveness”, identifying European (i) weaknesses in global innovation and, consequently, in global market impact, as well as (ii) regulatory overburden, the term competitiveness has been propelled into massive popularity. For instance, competitiveness has been established as a core guiding principle for the work of the European Commission (the competitiveness compass as a new roadmap for EU economic policy. But what does competitiveness exactly mean and how does it relate to competition? This contribution addresses possible concepts of competitiveness and their relationship with concepts of competition. Furthermore, we compare current narratives surrounding the competition-competitiveness interrelation with stylized academic empirical evidence. We conclude that (i) it should always be explicitly specified which notion and concept of the term competitiveness is referred to, (ii) effective competitiveness policies must be competition-based (i.e., promote competitiveness through competition), (iii) a selective firm- or industry-focused competitiveness policy is likely to decrease welfare in a world where lobbyism, rent-seeking, and imperfect political incentives are prevalent, (iv) narratives that we have experienced a specifically competition-centric era during the last decades are not supported by scientific findings, and (v) competition policy and merger control should be reinvigorated to promote public interest goals such as social welfare and economic resilience.

detail.abstract: This study examines strategic approaches to state asset management aimed at enhancing Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) and strengthening fiscal sustainability in Indonesia. It develops an analytical framework for optimizing state asset utilization through the application of the Highest and Best Use (HBU) principle, while also exploring implementation strategies, success factors, coordination mechanisms, and the integration of digital technologies. A qualitative methodology was employed, incorporating a Systematic Literature Review, Focus Group Discussions with government officials and asset managers, and NVivo-assisted thematic analysis. The data collection process identified operational challenges and strategic opportunities within Indonesia's state asset management ecosystem. Findings reveal four critical dimensions for effective state asset management: (1) the implementation of good governance principles integrated with public finance management to generate both economic returns and social benefits; (2) the development of specialized expertise among State-Owned Asset (BMN) managers; (3) regulatory reform to simplify administrative procedures while enhancing transparency; and (4) the formulation of integrated management strategies aligned with national priorities through inter-agency synergy and collaboration with the private sector. Recommendations include institutionalizing good governance within asset management frameworks, empowering the State Asset Management Agency (LMAN) as a central coordination mechanism, accelerating the digitalization of asset information systems, implementing comprehensive capacity development programs, and pursuing targeted regulatory reforms. Future research should explore opportunities for technological integration and conduct comparative analyses with international best practices. This research contributes to the field by synthesizing the Highest and Best Use (HBU) methodology with governance principles in the management of state assets. The proposed framework offers evidence-based guidance for optimizing state asset utilization and enhancing non-tax revenue streams, thereby strengthening Indonesia's fiscal sustainability while supporting broader economic development goals.

detail.abstract: Modern organizations, while structured for performance, often fail to address the fundamental human need for purpose and meaning, leading to widespread dissatisfaction. This paper introduces the IPPO (Interest, Personality, Philosophy, Outcome) model, an interdisciplinary framework designed to bridge this gap. Drawing on Erik Erikson's psychosocial stages, Viktor Frankl's Logotherapy, and Nietzschean existentialism, the model posits that core life philosophy is the primary determinant of well-being and performance. We outline an organizational methodology consisting of five phases: Discover, Analyze, Interpret, Activate, and Sustain. By implementing tools such as the IPPO Scorecard and Culture Heatmap, organizations can foster "purpose compatibility" rather than just productivity. Empirical evidence suggests that philosophical alignment is essential for improving job satisfaction, career adaptability, and psychological resilience.

detail.abstract: Women's health remains under-resourced, underprioritized, and narrowly defined. Across the life course, women experience distinct health needs with significant implications for health and wellbeing, yet persistent gaps in evidence and data continue to reinforce inequities. In the absence of a universally accepted definition of women's health, this study aimed to develop a topic map to capture its breadth and to identify an evidence-informed set of the top ten priority questions to guide future women's health research and innovation. We used a participatory, iterative methodology inspired by the 100 Questions Initiative, combining structured stakeholder engagement, rapid evidence synthesis, and iterative validation. An initial topic map was developed through an in-person workshop and refined through ongoing engagement with 77 global experts in women's health and data science. Guided by the topic map, experts submitted research questions via a virtual survey, which were refined, clustered, prioritized, and ranked. The topic map served as a shared framework to guide the submission of actionable research questions and comprised four branches: (1) key domains of women's health; (2) determinants and barriers; (3) technology and innovation; and (4) research and evidence gaps. A total of 113 questions were submitted, clustered into 56 themes, and narrowed to a top ten through expert prioritization, followed by public ranking. The highest-ranked questions focused on reframing and prioritizing women's health, strengthening investment and innovation ecosystems, and addressing evidence gaps, research participation, data quality, and equity. This study presents a comprehensive topic map that captures the complexity of women's health and provides a unifying framework for the field. The prioritized questions offer a strategic foundation to guide future research, policy, and investment to advance women's health innovation.

detail.abstract: This chapter, published here https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009605533.012 in the Cambridge University Press volume "The Politics of Corporations in 'New' India," edited by Rohit Varman, explores the reasons for the Indian business responses to Hindutva which have ranged from silence to open support. The essay considers material interests and greed as well as fear of reprisal from vindictive state agencies as well as the identity of corporate owners, professionals, and customers that align the interests of businesses with the regime. detail.abstract: Recent research shows that corporate disclosures are important in the interaction between firms and labor markets. Yet, empirical evidence on how labor market dynamics affect corporate disclosure practices behavior remains limited. Exploiting newly available firm-year and firmpair-year measures of labor market competition, we show that firms facing greater labor market competition adjust their disclosures in ways consistent with strategic labor market signaling. Firms with more labor market competition also align their disclosures more closely with labormarket peers, suggesting that competition for labor is associated with a convergence in disclosure practices. Together, our findings highlight labor market competition as an important and previously unexplored determinant of corporate disclosure practices.

detail.abstract: Philosophical and cultural studies aim to explore the structure, functions, and role of culture within society. Specifically, the philosophy of cultural phenomena seeks to identify key evolutionary cultural trends and understand the causes of crisis phenomena. To analyze these processes, a periodization of philosophical doctrines has been carried out, allowing for a systematic understanding of cultural development. It is argued that the synergy between philosophy and culture forms a unique reflexive and conceptual foundation for the cultural advancement of society, providing integrity, orderliness, and the rationalization of individual elements within the social system. The study also considers cultural and human activity through a historical and philosophical lens, highlighting the evolution of social development over time. The research demonstrates that traditional models of philosophical knowledge, aligned with order, balance, stability, and determinism, are increasingly inadequate in addressing the complexities of the modern world, characterized by chaos, imbalance, instability, and variability. Nonetheless, ideas derived from synergism retain significant paradigmatic relevance today. The philosophical nature of cultural aspects is interpreted as the development of the human position within historical and temporal contexts, emphasizing the logic of philosophical concepts in shaping societal cultural progress. The study also examines the interaction between social and cultural advancement, considering the challenges posed by globalization. Cultural dynamics are identified as a form of self-organization of meanings and values within the social space, closely linked to technological modernization. Four principal philosophical dimensions of cultural evolution are formulated: anthropological, ethicalreflecting emerging moral guidelines amid cultural pluralism-ontological, and epistemological. A model of cultural dynamics as a synergistic process integrating tradition, innovation, and value exchange is proposed. Comparative analysis shows that philosophical approaches offer a more comprehensive understanding of cultural evolution than purely sociological models. The concept of "cultural balance" is introduced as a prerequisite for sustainable societal development, ensuring a harmonious integration of traditions, values, and innovations, thereby fostering social stability, sustainable development, and global competitiveness.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how parent company resource allocation strategies influence group-level total factor productivity (TFP) within business groups, with particular attention to the moderating effects of subsidiary traits such as autonomy and diversification. Based on a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms with controlling subsidiaries from 2007 to 2022, we employ a two-way fixed effects model to assess how resource allocation influences group-level TFP, while considering the moderating roles of subsidiary autonomy and diversification. We also implement a comprehensive suite of robustness assessments, including alternative measurement strategies, placebo analyses, and instrumental variable estimations. Our findings suggest that a resource allocation strategy oriented toward operating assets is positively associated with group-level TFP. However, this positive effect diminishes in the presence of greater subsidiary autonomy and diversification. Further analysis indicates that operating asset-oriented resource allocation fosters innovation investment, which subsequently enhances boosts group-level TFP. Moreover, this mechanism is more salient in regions with higher levels of marketization, in cities characterized by stronger innovation capacity, and within industries facing more intense competition. The findings extend the Resource-based View to the business group context, contributing both theoretically and practically by informing the optimization of resource allocation strategies to enhance overall group performance.

detail.abstract: The article describes the processes of nomination, which are relevant for modern linguistics and are based on metaphorization of reality. The aim of the article is to study the cognitive aspects of metaphorization in modern European languages. The article describes the process of metaphorization in language through the imposition of secondary meaning on the primary one; describes the process of forming a linguistic picture of the world that is unique for each language community; investigates metaphorization at different levels of language (lexical, phrasal, phraseological); describes the peculiarities of metaphorization of neologisms based on the analysis of corpora of English and Polish texts. The article is based on the syncretism of descriptive, comparative, synthesis and analysis methods, systematic method in combination with the method of generalization. It is shown that the modification of metaphorical models occurs mainly due to the involvement of neologisms as a source of metaphorization, the activation of such established semantic spheres as high technology, economics and finance, and mass culture in this function. In European languages, the main cognitive structures are dominated by substantive metaphor, whose function is to nominate new realities of the surrounding reality. Due to the analytical nature of the English language, a significant number of partial metaphors function in it, realized with the help of complex words and stable phrases. Metaphors-neologisms are found in different styles of speech: scientific, formal business, journalistic, colloquial. It has been established that the linguistic picture of the world presented in the metaphorical subsystems of English and Polish is anthropocentric in nature, since one of the most productive areas of metaphorization is the human being. It has been determined that in the field of communication, linguistic metaphor in English and Polish fulfills all the functions traditionally attributed to it, i.e. communicative, nominative, expressive and characteristic. In the studied European languages, all the traditionally distinguished types of metaphor are observed, i.e. metonymy, hyperbole, euphemism, periphrasis. Metaphor is used to evaluate reality, express the speaker's attitude to the surrounding realities of the world, and form the cognitive (mental) and linguistic worldviews of speakers.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the ethical dimensions inherent in the teaching of English as a second or foreign language (ESL/EFL), emphasizing the moral responsibilities educators bear in fostering inclusive, equitable, and culturally sensitive learning environments. Drawing on ethical frameworks such as virtue ethics, deontology, and consequentialism, the study examines key issues including cultural bias in curricula, the promotion of linguistic diversity versus standardization, and the ethical implications of assessment practices that may perpetuate inequalities. Through a qualitative analysis of case studies from diverse educational contexts, including classrooms in Asia, Europe, and North America, the research highlights how ethical decision-making in pedagogy can mitigate power imbalances and enhance learner autonomy. Findings reveal that integrating ethical values-such as respect, fairness, and social justice-into teaching strategies not only improves educational outcomes but also contributes to broader societal goals of intercultural understanding. The paper concludes with recommendations for teacher training programs to incorporate ethical reflection, underscoring the need for ongoing dialogue in the field to address emerging challenges like digital ethics in online language instruction. This work contributes to the discourse on professional ethics in language education, advocating for a pedagogy that prioritizes human dignity alongside linguistic proficiency.

detail.title: Basic Concepts of Ethics, Morals, and the Profession
detail.abstract: The concepts of Morals, Ethics, and Profession are three fundamental pillars that form the framework for individual and group behavior, particularly in professional work environments. A comprehensive understanding of these three concepts is crucial to creating a society and professional practice that is responsible, fair, and high in integrity. Morality (or Morality) refers to the personal values and beliefs that distinguish between right and wrong in individual behavior. It is often internal, based on conscience, tradition, or religious teachings, and serves as a basic compass in everyday decision-making. Ethics is the systematic study and philosophical reflection on morality. Ethics serves as a set of socially or professionally agreed-upon principles or standards for governing behavior. In a general context, ethics are rules of conduct derived from external sources (e.g., professional codes of conduct). Ethics is divided into three main branches: metaethics (the origins and meaning of ethical concepts), normative ethics (practical moral standards for determining correct behavior), and applied ethics (the application of moral standards in specific situations, such as business or medicine). A profession is defined not simply as an occupation, but as one that requires specialized education, intensive training, and a commitment to public service. The key characteristics of a profession include: a structured body of knowledge, autonomy in practice, and, most importantly, a Code of Professional Ethics.

detail.abstract: This Article presents the first comprehensive 50-state analysis of state constitutional provisions applicable to wrongful convictions and their relationship to compensation statutes. Drawing on data from the National Registry of Exonerations documenting 3,698 exonerations since 1989,¹ this research reveals a constitutional paradox: states officially document their wrongful convictions through participation in national databases while simultaneously denying meaningful remedies to the innocent. As of October 2025, only 38 states and the District of Columbia provide statutory compensation, leaving 12 states with no compensation framework whatsoever.² This Article argues that state constitutions-interpreted independently from increasingly restrictive federal precedent-provide a viable path forward. Many state constitutions contain provisions with no federal analogue, use distinct textual formulations, and have their own interpretive histories that support broader protections than federal due process doctrine.³ The "Documentation Paradox" framework demonstrates that states' official recognition of wrongful convictions through exoneration registries establishes documented knowledge of systemic failures, transforming negligent denial of compensation into intentional constitutional violations under state law. The Article develops a typology of state constitutional provisions relevant to wrongful convictions, analyzes empirical patterns in exoneration and compensation data, and provides state-specific litigation roadmaps for deploying state constitutional claims. This framework is particularly critical for Black and brown exonerees, who face official misconduct at higher rates and are seven times more likely than white Americans to be wrongfully convicted of serious crimes.⁴

title: Digital Data as Dual-Value Assets: Shadow Banking as the Primary Financial Pathway and Commercial Banks as Dependent Amplifiers in China’s Digital Financing Networks

detail.title: Digital Data as Dual-Value Assets: Shadow Banking as the Primary Financial Pathway and Commercial Banks as Dependent Amplifiers in China’s Digital Financing Networks
detail.abstract: This study proposes a new mechanism to explain how digital data create financial value in emerging digital economies. Existing literature has emphasized the role of digitalization in reducing information frictions, but has not distinguished between who provides financing and how data are transformed into credit. Based on observations from China’s digital transaction networks, this paper identifies a dual-value structure of data assets: a primary financial pathway through shadow banking and a secondary pathway through commercial banks. Shadow banking institutions—platform firms, factoring companies, and other non-bank financial intermediaries—use digitally exposed transaction flows to perform real-time verification, providing the core channel of data-driven financing. Commercial banks, in contrast, rely on these verified data to convert future cash flows into pledgeable, auditable assets, making bank financing a dependent amplification effect rather than an independent mechanism. This dual-pathway framework clarifies the formation of data’s financial value and offers a structural explanation for China’s unique credit creation process in the digital era.
