title: Machiavellian Marketing: The Necessary Evolution of Persuasion, Power, and Digital Propaganda

detail.title: Machiavellian Marketing: The Necessary Evolution of Persuasion, Power, and Digital Propaganda
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Machiavellian Marketing as an emerging strategic doctrine; a school of thought that combines psychology, narrative engineering, and platform-specific persuasion to shape audience perception and consumer behavior in the algorithmic age. Unlike conventional marketing methods that prioritize visibility or brand aesthetics, Machiavellian Marketing concerns itself with power: the ability to engineer attention, control narrative environments, and influence belief before a consumer becomes aware of the mechanism shaping their decision. Drawing from The Machiavellian Marketing Framework™ (MMF), The 23 Laws of Marketing, propaganda theory, and platform-based psychological design, this doctrine argues that modern marketing is no longer a contest of products, but a contest of perception. Platforms like Pinterest demonstrate that marketing functions as a psychological marketplace, where desire, belief, and narrative, not advertising, drive outcomes. As algorithms increasingly become the arbiters of culture and commerce, Machiavellian Marketing provides the blueprint for dominance in the attention economy: to architect environments rather than compete within them.

title: Analysis of the Successes and Limitations on the Path of Digitalization of the Russian Economy
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO University)

detail.title: Analysis of the Successes and Limitations on the Path of Digitalization of the Russian Economy
detail.abstract: The purpose of the work is to study the achievements and limitations on the path of digitalization of the Russian economy. The object of research is the digital economy. Research methods: information analysis and synthesis, comparison, dynamic analysis. The article analyzes the main achievements of digitalization in Russia: the development of Internet communications, increased employment, venture capital, the effectiveness of investments in information technology, and the creation of digital interaction services. Among the grievances of digitalization are the reduction of technology, the blocking and unavailability of foreign services and websites, the imposition of sanctions, and the shortage of personnel in the information technology industry. It can be concluded that the digitalization of the Russian economy has slowed down significantly in recent years. The successes achieved in the 2000s and 2010s currently make it possible to maintain digital development at a high level. Despite this, the digital development of the economy may almost completely stop within 5-10 years due to the obsolescence of the ICT infrastructure, the shortage of personnel and the inability to import technologies. Among the most significant development prospects, a number of areas can be identified: the creation of a sustainable scientific, technical and educational base; development of Russian analogues of foreign technologies and services; creation of drivers for retaining IT specialists in the economy.

title: The Uneven Economics of Protests: Understanding Social Unrest and Income Dynamics in Pakistan
affiliations: , University of the Punjab (PU) - Department of Economics and Government College University Lahore

detail.title: The Uneven Economics of Protests: Understanding Social Unrest and Income Dynamics in Pakistan
detail.abstract: This paper studies how social unrest shapes income outcomes across districts in Pakistan. Using district-level panel data from 2011 to 2021, it combines household income information from the Pakistan Social and Living Standards Measurement Survey (PSLM/HIES) with detailed records of protests and political violence from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED). The analysis applies fixed-effects and quantile panel regression techniques to capture how the economic effects of unrest vary across districts with different income levels. The results show that protests and riots are associated with higher incomes in relatively better-off districts, suggesting that organized collective action can enhance bargaining power and economic responsiveness where institutions and markets are stronger. In contrast, violence against civilians and high-intensity remote violence consistently reduce incomes, with the largest losses occurring in poorer districts that lack economic resilience. Strategic developments are linked to income gains, but these benefits are uneven and concentrated in already advantaged regions. Overall, the findings indicate that unrest is not uniformly harmful or beneficial; its economic consequences depend on the type of unrest and the local economic context. Policies that distinguish between peaceful civic mobilization and destructive violence, and that account for district-level inequalities, are essential for promoting more inclusive economic outcomes.

title: The Paradox of "Authenticity" in Modern Marketing: When Transparency Becomes Strategy

detail.title: The Paradox of "Authenticity" in Modern Marketing: When Transparency Becomes Strategy
detail.abstract: In contemporary marketing, "authenticity" is treated as a moral virtue. Yet functionally, it operates as a perception strategy. Whether genuine or engineered, authenticity is a curated performance governed by selective disclosure, emotional framing, and identity construction. Modern research in social psychology (Goffman, 1959; Snyder, 1987) confirms that individuals manage impressions instinctively, while recent findings in digital behavior show that audiences reward polished vulnerability over unfiltered truth. This commentary argues that authenticity has evolved from a personal ideal into a Machiavellian device: a tool for influence, trust acceleration, and rapid audience capture. By analyzing the psychological mechanisms behind self-presentation, parasocial bonding, and narrative framing, this paper positions "engineered authenticity" not as deception, but as a strategic necessity in an algorithmic ecosystem where attention is scarce and perception is power. This commentary examines how the pursuit of authenticity moved from moral virtue to strategic currency, why the illusion of transparency now outperforms traditional branding, and how this dynamic aligns with Machiavelli's long-standing lesson: it is often more useful to appear virtuous than to be virtuous.

title: The Great Replacement: Labor and AI Policy in China and the U.S.

detail.title: The Great Replacement: Labor and AI Policy in China and the U.S.
detail.abstract: In the hypothetical case of the “Great Replacement” of human workers by AI, which has been projected by some scholars, a widespread increase in unemployment rates would seemingly mark a permanent shift in workforce patterns in contrast to previous  exogenous shocks like the COVID-19 pandemic. Even though new jobs related to AI would be created as well, it is unreasonable to expect that these jobs would make up for all of the jobs that are eliminated due to AI, and it is also unlikely that workers made redundant by AI would be capable of fulfilling these new roles without a massive investment in training programs. Thus, many countries are already plannninng for this eventuality by exploring or planning retraining programs specifically for workers displaced by AI. However, in order for such programs to be successful, they must account for the new realities of the AI economy, in which many skills or jobs may not be "AI retrainable" due to the constant improvements in AI capabilities. This article summarizes some of the challenges in retraining workers displaced by AI in the world's two largest economies and the world's preeminent AI powers, namely China and the U.S.

title: Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth in Nigeria: The Imperative of a Rules-Based Neutral Fiscal Stance

detail.title: Achieving Sustainable Economic Growth in Nigeria: The Imperative of a Rules-Based Neutral Fiscal Stance

declarations.ethicsApproval: The author declares that this research did not involve human participants, animal subjects, or the collection of sensitive personal data. This study is based on the analysis of publicly available macroeconomic datasets from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Consequently, the study is exempt from institutional ethical review requirements (IRB), as all data utilized in the econometric analysis are aggregated and anonymized at the source. The author also confirms that the data analyzed in this manuscript—spanning the 36-year period from 1990 to 2025—are authentic and have not been manipulated to bias the reported econometric results or the structural gap analysis. The integrity of the multivariate regression and the resulting spending elasticity of 0.702 is maintained throughout the study. The author utilized generative AI tools solely for the purpose of technical language editing and structural formatting to ensure the clarity and international readability of the manuscript. The conceptual framework (Neutral Fiscal Stance), the econometric modeling (Multivariate OLS First-Difference), and the specific policy recommendations (LTROP and SWF reforms) were developed entirely by the authors. The authors take full responsibility for the accuracy, integrity, and conclusions of the final work.

detail.abstract: This article investigates the structural roots of chronic macroeconomic instability in Nigeria, positing that the Nigeria's failure to achieve sustainable growth is fundamentally deeply rooted in its pro-cyclical policy regime. Utilizing a multivariate econometric framework over the period 1990-2025, the article establishes a statistically significant causal nexus between volatile oil revenue shocks and discretionary government expenditure. Empirical evidence reveal a high spending elasticity of 0.702, indicating that a 1% surge in oil revenue growth precipitates a 0.70% acceleration in public spending. This relationship has culminated in an "Ultimate Policy Failure" by 2025, characterized by a total fiscal decoupling where budgeted expenditure (₦32.5 trillion) stands at 6.1 times the long-term sustainable revenue level, necessitating debt and tax instruments to fund 83.7% of the total budget. To mitigate this fiscal pathology, the paper advocates for an institutional transition toward a rules-based "Neutral Fiscal Stance" anchored in the Permanent Income Hypothesis (PIH). Through a comparative evaluation of the Norwegian and Chilean fiscal models, we provide a robust policy blueprint tailored for the Nigerian context. Central to this proposal is the legislative adoption of a non-discretionary Long-Term Reference Oil Price (LTROP) and the institutionalization of the Sovereign Wealth Fund as an automatic stabilization mechanism. These reforms are posited as nonnegotiable structural prerequisites for insulating the domestic economy from external shocks, curbing unsustainable debt accumulation, and unlocking long-term economic diversification.

title: Logistics, Resilience, and AI-ESG: Pathways to Export Competitiveness under Global Value Chain Restructuring

detail.title: Logistics, Resilience, and AI-ESG: Pathways to Export Competitiveness under Global Value Chain Restructuring
detail.abstract: This study examines how Vietnamese export firms sustain competitiveness amid the restructuring of global value chains shaped by protectionism, de-globalization, and the twin green–digital transitions. Drawing on a survey of 200 firms and applying Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Logit regression, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and Panel Fixed Effects (Panel FE), the analysis focuses on three pillars: (i) logistics and Domestic Value Added (DVA), (ii) resilience and supplier networks, and (iii) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG). Results show that logistics digitalization reduces tariff pass-through, while compliance with Rules of Origin (ROO) lowers the effective tariff rate, enabling firms to exploit Free Trade Agreement (FTA) preferences. Resilience and supplier density enhance order retention and contribute to higher DVA. AI improves Total Factor Productivity (TFP), ESG strengthens contract sustainability, and their interaction (AI × ESG) yields complementary gains in profit margins. The study highlights the need for firms to combine localization, resilience, and innovation, alongside synchronized green–digital policies at the state level.

title: Ethical Excellence and the Donkey as a Transformational Model: The P.E.S.A. Academic Theory

detail.title: Ethical Excellence and the Donkey as a Transformational Model: The P.E.S.A. Academic Theory
detail.abstract: This study introduces the P.E.S.A. theory (Performance, Ethics, Sacrifice, Action), a novel conceptual framework for analyzing moral development through a Heptagonal Ethical Scale. By employing the ethologically grounded concept of the "natural donkey" as a zero-reference point for behavioral authenticity (fitra), the theory maps the progression from cognitive negligence to systemic transformational leadership. Adopting a theoretical and integrative methodology, this work synthesizes insights from moral philosophy, neuroscience, behavioral economics, and sociology. It argues that moral integrity, as modeled by this scale, is a fundamental driver of long-term societal sustainability and provides a diagnostic tool for assessing ethical maturation.

title:
The Pioneer's Trap: Why Market Leaders Fail to Respond to Visible Competitive Threats
A Strategic Autopsy of iRobot Corporation (2018-2025)
affiliations: Babson College

detail.title:
The Pioneer's Trap: Why Market Leaders Fail to Respond to Visible Competitive Threats
A Strategic Autopsy of iRobot Corporation (2018-2025)
detail.abstract: Context: On December 14, 2025, iRobot Corporation, inventor of the robotic vacuum category and holder of 75% North American market share as recently as 2020, filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The company will be acquired by Shenzhen Picea Robotics, its Chinese contract manufacturer, through a debt-for-equity swap valued at approximately $264 million in forgiven debt. Purpose: This paper investigates why category-creating firms fail to respond to competitive threats they clearly perceive. Existing literature on disruption focuses on incumbents who fail to see threats; this paper examines the distinct phenomenon of leaders who see threats but cannot act. Method: Single-case longitudinal study using public financial filings (SEC 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEFM14A), executive interviews, regulatory documents, and technical analysis spanning 2018-2025. Findings: The paper identifies four interconnected "Pioneer's Traps" that create response paralysis: (1) Technical Dogma, identity-based commitment to a technological paradigm; (2) Competitor Mislabeling, misclassifying rivals as low-tech copycats; (3) M&A Dependency, strategic paralysis during acquisition pendency; and (4) the Manufacturing Boomerang, value migration from brand-holder to contract manufacturer. Contribution: Extends disruption theory by distinguishing "awareness failure" from "response failure" and proposes a diagnostic framework for identifying institutional decline before terminal phase.

title: GIFfluence: A Visual Approach to Investor Sentiment and the Stock Market
affiliations: University of California, Irvine, University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business - Finance and Business Economics Department, UCLA Anderson School of Management and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen - School of Management and Economics

detail.title: GIFfluence: A Visual Approach to Investor Sentiment and the Stock Market
detail.abstract: We study dynamic visual representations as a proxy for investor sentiment about the stock market. Our sentiment index, GIFsentiment, is constructed from millions of posts in the Graphics Interchange Format (GIF) on a leading investment social media platform. GIFsentiment correlates with seasonal mood variations and the severity of COVID lockdowns. It is positively associated with contemporaneous market returns and negatively predicts returns for up to four weeks, even after controlling for other sentiment and attention measures. These effects are stronger among portfolios that are more susceptible to mispricing. GIFsentiment positively predicts trading volume, market volatility, and flows toward equity funds and away from debt funds. Our evidence suggests that GIFsentiment is a proxy for misperceptions that are later corrected.

title: A Short Horizon Model for Commodity Futures Prices

detail.title: A Short Horizon Model for Commodity Futures Prices
detail.abstract: A one-factor stochastic process is proposed to model the short horizon dynamics of commodity futures prices under the theory of storage and the assumption that spot prices follow an arithmetic Brownian motion. The contribution to the existing literature is to present an alternative view to log-normal models in which the discounted expected value of the spot price maintains its martingale property under the risk-neutral measure but where: i) the price follows a normal distribution instead of its log-returns and ii) the price of futures contracts can be negative. Moreover, the model can also be used to obtain closed form solutions for the price of European options on futures without losing mathematical tractability. Finally, the model performance is tested on individual platinum futures contract to illustrate that it is a more appropriate representation for its short horizon dynamics than a similar log-normal model.

title: Why, how and when does food loss and waste occur in Moroccan households? Insights from wheat-based products
affiliations: Sultan Moulay Slimane University, Ibn Zohr University, Ibn Zohr University, Ibn Zohr University, Ibn Zohr University, Ibn Zohr University, Sultan Moulay Slimane University, Ibn Zohr University, Ibn Zohr University, Sultan Moulay Slimane University and Sultan Moulay Slimane University

detail.title: Why, how and when does food loss and waste occur in Moroccan households? Insights from wheat-based products
detail.abstract: Food Loss and Waste (FLW) at the household level remains underexplored, as most studies overlook detailed flows and critical points within households. This paper revolutionizes the commonly used terminology by challenging the conventional distinction between "losses" and "wastes" demonstrating that an important portion of "losses" can also occur at the household level. It proposes a refined framework distinguishing three consumption modes: Take-Away (TA), Home-Prepared (HP), and Food Service (FS), while also introducing the neglected dimension of post-storage waste, examined through a life-cycle perspective. Data were collected for 17 representative products using a diary-based approach. Principal Component Analyses identified income, education, urban residence as positively correlated with higher FLW, while the presence of housewife and household size showed negative effects. A Sankey flow analysis revealed that households receive over 1,110 kg annually, with around 9.4% lost or wasted. Waste rates vary across consumption modes: TA (6.03%), HP (11.09%) and FS (22.74%), highlighting distinct intervention priorities. Complementary Sunburst  and Treemap analysis identified product-specific vulnerabilities, with Bread emerging as major contributor. By combining conceptual innovation and empirical quantification through detailed diary-based flow tracking, determinant analysis, and complementary visual tools, this study not only measures household FLW but also identifies strategic points, offering pathways to promote food sustainability through targeted social and behavioral innovations.

title: Competition in the Clouds: Emerging Clouds of Sovereignty on the Horizons of Digital Markets and Data Act
affiliations: Maastricht University

detail.title: Competition in the Clouds: Emerging Clouds of Sovereignty on the Horizons of Digital Markets and Data Act

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Cloud computing, that emerged as an early response to outsourcing by small and mid-sized firms, has over time, emerged as the foundation of the data economy. The dependence on cloud is anticipated to strengthen further, as AI and quantum computing become central to the big data-driven digital economy. The global markets for cloud are controlled by three hyperscalers, Amazon, Microsoft and Google. What technical (such as complexity of the technology, learning effects and interoperability) and economic considerations (such as ecosystem effects, egress fee and lock-in) can potentially explain the enduring global dominance of the three hyperscalers? In addition to the economic consideration, cloud also has key non-economic dimensions, such as sovereignty and innovation, factors that also reasonably explain a call by Nation States across the globe for workable competition, fairness and contestability in the cloud computing industry. This research contribution develops the foregoing considerations, and reasons that considering the infrastructural and foundational nature of cloud, it should be seen as part of a digital ecosystem owned and controlled by the hyperscalers, that also qualify as gatekeepers in the EU's Digital Markets Act, and other equivalent ex-ante regulatory frameworks across the globe. Following an evaluation of how qualitative considerations for designation may be more suited to qualify cloud under the DMA, the contribution looks at the portability and interoperability requirements under the Data Act. It also appraises how the Commission's Digital Omnibus package may contribute toward a more effective functioning of the Data Act, and thereby, promote competition in the clouds.

title: Promoting Ho Chi Minh City's Leading Role and Its Capacity to Connect Regional Industrial Value Chains

detail.title: Promoting Ho Chi Minh City's Leading Role and Its Capacity to Connect Regional Industrial Value Chains
detail.abstract: Following the administrative expansion through the merger with Bình Dương and Bà Rịa-Vũng Tàu, Ho Chi Minh City has formed an integrated industrial space with superior capabilities within the Southern Key Economic Region. This article analyzes the city's new role as the core coordinator of regional industrial value chains, clarifying the current distribution of industries, levels of specialization, and existing linkage-spillover mechanisms. The findings show that the merger of the three localities creates a foundation for integrated value chains, from R&D, design, and production to logistics and exportwhile enabling each province to shift from standalone development to functional specialization within a shared ecosystem. Based on this, the article proposes a model for organizing integrated production space, interregional coordination mechanisms, infrastructure connectivity development, and enterprise support. Ho Chi Minh City should transition from a localized growth center to a regional nucleus and diffusion axis, leading production assignment, logistics, and R&D for the entire region. Priority actions include establishing a regional coordination institution, investing in strategic infrastructure, connecting supply chains, strengthening FDI-domestic enterprise linkages, and developing satellite R&D networks. The study provides theoretical and practical foundations for a regional industrial development model oriented toward integration, coordination, and sustainability.

title: The Impact of Merit-Based Scholarships on Post-Secondary Outcomes: Evidence from Ontario

detail.title: The Impact of Merit-Based Scholarships on Post-Secondary Outcomes: Evidence from Ontario
detail.abstract: Merit-based scholarships have long been used by post-secondary institutions to make higher education more attractive and accessible to students by rewarding high performance. Despite their widespread use, empirical evidence on the effectiveness of such scholarships in achieving their objectives remains limited. This study employs a fuzzy regression discontinuity design to evaluate the impact of a large, lump-sum merit-based entrance scholarship on the enrolment rates of domestic undergraduate students at the University of Toronto. I find that being awarded a scholarship has no statistically significant effect on a student's likelihood of accepting their admission offer and enroling at the University. However, a heterogeneity analysis reveals a positive effect on enrolment rates among students from lower-income neighborhoods and those residing farther from the University of Toronto, highlighting the potential benefits of a more targeted scholarship design. Furthermore, the analysis suggests that a student's prior preference for the institution influences their responsiveness to scholarship incentives. This finding underscores the persistence of college preferences and raises questions about the efficacy of merit-based scholarships in shaping enrolment decisions.

title: Falsifiable Estimation of Low-Frequency Correlation Times in Precision Detectors: A Portable Workflow with Explicit Failure Modes
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Falsifiable Estimation of Low-Frequency Correlation Times in Precision Detectors: A Portable Workflow with Explicit Failure Modes
detail.abstract: Precision timing in large detectors and complex quantum-sensing systems is routinely limited by low-frequency fluctuations whose structure is easy to describe qualitatively and easy to mishandle quantitatively. In high-energy physics (HEP), slow timing wander and common-mode drifts propagate into calibration constants, degrade resolution, and entangle otherwise independent subsystems; recent performance notes make clear that a portable, auditable account of these effects is now a firstorder need. We present a falsifiable, frequency-domain workflow to estimate a defensible correlation time τc from one-sided, Parseval-normalized power spectra. The method instantiates a single-pole (Lorentzian) low-frequency hypothesis using two complementary estimators-a variance-invariant (VI) plateau method exploiting the flat low-frequency band, and a local knee refit of the Lorentzian spectrum on an adaptive window [a fc, b fc]. Each step is guarded by explicit, pre-registered tests: Parseval ratio verification, plateau slope flatness, Lorentzian fit quality (R 2), and agreement between VI and knee estimates. Any failure triggers a status=reject with machine-readable rationale rather than forced scalar output. When both branches pass, a fixed 0.8/0.2 consensus (VI/knee) approximates inverse-variance weighting across practical record lengths. For multichannel records, we project the cross-spectral matrix onto its leading low-frequency mode only when coherence and eigenvector stability make that projection identifiable, and we reapply the same gates to the pooled spectrum before reporting. All decisions and thresholds are logged to a "null catalog" CSV alongside pre-registration YAML, enabling downstream audit without reading source code. Monte Carlo validation on OU surrogates demonstrates bias < 6% under weak 1/f β contamination (strength ≤ 0.3) and principled rejection when gates trip. The workflow's novelty lies not in claiming the Lorentzian form-single-pole spectra have long pedigree-but in operationalizing that claim to travel between facilities, experiments, and disciplines while maintaining falsifiability as a first-class objective.

title: An Examination of Bitcoin's Structural Shortcomings as Money: A Synthesis of Economic and Technical Critiques

detail.title: An Examination of Bitcoin's Structural Shortcomings as Money: A Synthesis of Economic and Technical Critiques

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study relies exclusively on publicly available secondary data and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Since its inception, Bitcoin has been positioned as a revolutionary alternative to national currencies, attracting immense public and academic interest. This paper presents a critical evaluation of this claim, suggesting that Bitcoin faces significant structural barriers to qualifying as money. It synthesizes critiques from two distinct schools of economic thought-Post-Keynesianism and the Austrian School-and validating their conclusions with rigorous technical analysis. From a Post-Keynesian perspective, it is argued that Bitcoin does not function as money because it is not a debt-based IOU and fails to exhibit the essential properties required for a stable monetary asset [Vianna, 2021]. Concurrently, from an Austrian viewpoint, it is shown to be inconsistent with a strict interpretation of Mises's Regression Theorem, as it lacks prior non-monetary value and has not achieved the status of the most saleable commodity [Peniaz and Kavaliou, 2024]. These theoretical arguments are then supported by an empirical analysis of Bitcoin's extreme volatility, hard-coded scalability limits, fragile market structure, and insecure long-term economic design. The paper concludes that Bitcoin is more accurately characterized as a novel speculative asset whose primary legacy may be the technological innovation it has spurred, rather than its viability as a monetary standard [Lo and Wang, 2014].

title: Brazil's Humanitarian Diplomacy: Key Trends
affiliations: MGIMO University

detail.title: Brazil's Humanitarian Diplomacy: Key Trends
detail.abstract: This article analyzes the key trends and characteristics of Brazil's humanitarian diplomacy as a donor country. It focuses on its fundamental differences from Western models, expressed in its emphasis on horizontal South-South partnerships, unconditional technical cooperation, and solidarity diplomacy. It also examines the institutional foundations, ideological motivations, and internal challenges of this policy, including its high dependence on political developments in the country.

title: Robust (Decentralized) Oracle Design

detail.title: Robust (Decentralized) Oracle Design
detail.abstract: An oracle is a node that supplies blockchain smart contracts with external information that the blockchain itself cannot access. However, the oracle problem of ensuring that such information is accurate and resistant to manipulation remains a fundamental challenge. In this paper, I investigate the design of compensation mechanisms and aggregation methods for decentralized oracle networks consisting of adversarial and strategic nodes, to incentivize truthful reporting and robustly aggregate dispersed information into a consensus. I establish an impossibility result: Under a mild condition, fully decentralized robust compensation mechanisms-under which truthful reporting constitutes a strict Nash equilibrium for strategic nodes regardless of adversarial reporting strategies-do not exist. I then show that if the designer can occasionally access a verified signal about the ground truth, a simple squared-loss-based mechanism restores truth reporting as a dominant strategy. On the aggregation side, I show that the empirical coordinate-wise median widely used in practice may fail even without an adversary and ignores the intrinsically high-dimensional structure of decentralized oracle networks. By contrast, adversarial nodes that appear normal in every single dimension can be detected from a "global" view using high-dimensional robust machine learning algorithms, which yield a consensus with strong error guarantees.

title: Tariffs, Margins, and the Export Response: ECOWAS at Europe's Gate

detail.title: Tariffs, Margins, and the Export Response: ECOWAS at Europe's Gate
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies how EU tariff cuts transmit to export performance among ECOWAS economies by embedding tariff variation into a gravity-model panel with country-pair fixed effects. Using logged trade values and multiple estimators (OLS, FE, RE, BE) alongside a Hausman test, the analysis isolates an elasticity whereby a 1% reduction in EU import tariffs is associated with roughly a 0.487% rise in ECOWAS exports. Robustness comes from cross-specification stability and diagnostic tests, translating into policy-relevant guidance on sequencing liberalization to unlock extensive-margin participation and product scope expansion. While observational rather than experimental, the design maps tariff policy to export competitiveness with transparency on assumptions and limitations, informing negotiations and preference schemes between the EU and West African partners.

title: Quantifying Investor-Driven Overvaluation in the Australian Housing Market: An Empirical Demand Attribution Price Model

detail.title: Quantifying Investor-Driven Overvaluation in the Australian Housing Market: An Empirical Demand Attribution Price Model
detail.abstract: This paper presents an empirical model to calculate overvaluation of the Australian established housing market sector from 1999 to the present, a period marked by sustained investor demand supported by three generous tax concessions. The price model is intrinsically expressed in the economic fundamental: in a supply limited market demand drives prices up, housing buyer and price data allow market specific implementation of the model and in Australia's case established housing supply is essentially fixed. Furthermore, buyers account for economic factors in their decision to buy or not along with the bank's decision to lend or not to buyers. The model attributes marginal real house price movements to buyer types: first home buyers, non first home buyer owner-occupiers, and investors. By correlating demand shifts in each group with corresponding price changes, the model attributes the proportion of price inflation driven by buyer type. While all buyer type demand contributes to house price inflation, only the investor-attributable portion is treated as overvaluation, as it is driven primarily by tax distortions and expectations of future capital gains rather than housing consumption needs. This direct approach analysis indicates that approximately 46% of real house prices at the end of 2024 was attributable to investorinduced speculative demand which equates to an 84% overvaluation in the established housing market. The evolution of this overvaluation meets Nobel Laureate Joseph Stiglitz's definition of an asset bubble with one caveat, it is a rational bubble so long as investors believe the tax concessions will remain in place for the long term, a belief grounded not in economics but in historical political mandate.

title: EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF ZILLOW HOME LOANS PRICING
affiliations: Georgetown University Law Center

detail.title: EMPIRICAL ANALYSIS OF ZILLOW HOME LOANS PRICING

declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by CoStar

publicationDetails.detailsText: Georgetown University Law Center Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: Georgetown University Law Center Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: The recent NAR antitrust settlement provides the opportunity for changes in home buyers’ relationships with buyer agents. At the same time, two recent class action cases have alleged that Zillow has engaged in deceptive conduct, including having its affiliated agents steer home buyers to borrow through its Zillow Home Loans (ZHL). The empirical analysis in this report examines whether ZHL loans have higher prices than other lenders, after controlling for borrower demographics, loan characteristics and other factors. The analysis uses the public Home Mortgage Disclosure Act database for loans originated in the 2022-2024 period. The empirical findings suggest that ZHL borrowers pay significantly higher mortgage costs than they would pay to other lenders, which are referred to as ZHL “overcharges.” The estimate of these overcharges on 30-year conventional loans for ZHL borrowers is a higher mortgage APR of approximately 10 basis points for the period 2022-2024, which amounts to a net present value (NPV) overcharge over the 30-year life of the loan of about $2,900 on an average loan size of about $321,000, and a higher mortgage APR of approximately 15 basis points for the year 2024, which amounts to a NPV overcharge of about $4,600 on an average loan size of about $337,000, as compared to borrowers with similar characteristics originating similar types of loans at other lenders.  The 2024 NPV dollar overcharge is higher than in earlier years both because of an increase in the incremental basis points and because the average loan size is increasing.  The estimates for VA and FHA loans also indicate significant NPV overcharges in 2024, though not earlier.  Additional analyses of 30-year conventional loans show that the difference between Zillow and other lenders’ APRs for a comparable loan is larger in percentage terms for lower-income borrowers for all three loan categories. Analysis of heterogeneity by race and ethnicity shows that the overcharges paid by Black borrowers are substantially larger than the overcharges paid by White non-Hispanic/Latino borrowers. Hispanic/Latino borrowers had an undercharge relative to other lenders in 2022 and 2023, but an overcharge in 2024.

title: Monetary Financing Prohibition, Inflation, Debt and the Rule of Law in the EU: a Legal, Philosophical, and Economic Inquiry into Treaty Constraints (Sobre o Financiamento Monetário)

detail.title: Monetary Financing Prohibition, Inflation, Debt and the Rule of Law in the EU: a Legal, Philosophical, and Economic Inquiry into Treaty Constraints (Sobre o Financiamento Monetário)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Professor Luís Silva Morais (deceased) and CIRSF (Centro de Investigação para a Regulação e Supervisão Financeira)
declarations.funderStatement: The research is independent. The author previously worked with CIRSF (Centro de Investigação para a Regulação e Supervisão Financeira) under the tutorship of Professor Luis Silva Morais until the latter's passing.

detail.abstract:
This independent interdisciplinary paper examines whether non-conventional monetary policies adopted within the European Monetary Union and operationalized through Open Market Operations have amounted, in practice, to inflationary monetary financing prohibited by the Treaties of the European Union, notably Article 123 TFEU. The study argues that, while nominal monetary authority must be normatively tied to real economic meaning to remain compatible with the constitutional principles of the rule of law, the legal separation between fiscal and monetary spheres functions as the ultimate safeguard of the EU deficit and debt rules, and that the extensive discretionary interpretation of central-bank mandates risks enabling hidden fiscal transfers and artificially price-inflationary demand for market instruments.

Drawing on legal governance principles, monetary-law foundations, inflation understood as the currency’s purchasing-power depreciation, and philosophical constraints of sovereignty under the rule of law, the paper contends that Member States bear a dual responsibility – to preserve the common currency as a system-wide unit of account, while acting within coordinated economic competences of the European Union economic governance. It further suggests that, within this institutional paradigm, bilateral agreements on euro usage are possible, but only legally coherent if fully aligned with internal and EU fiscal constraints.

Lastly, the analysis proposes a principled reform of the European Banking Union to ensure euro fungibility and a sustainable triadic equilibrium between price stability, financial stability, and competition.

title: Mapping of Google Business Categories to NACE Rev. 2 using Large Language Models

detail.title: Mapping of Google Business Categories to NACE Rev. 2 using Large Language Models
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the efficacy of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash, as well as a fine-tuning of XLM-RoBERTa for the automated mapping of Google Business Categories (GBCs) to the NACE Rev. 2 statistical classification of economic activities. Accurate mapping between these systems is crucial for economic analysis and data integration. We compare generated mappings against a human-coded ground truth dataset, achieving up to 90% accuracy. While these results are promising, we also analyze the limitations of the LLM approach and suggest avenues for future research, including a comparison with embedding-based methodologies.

title: Legal Regulation of the Mining Industry in Peru, Chile, and the Russian Federation: A Comparative Study

detail.title: Legal Regulation of the Mining Industry in Peru, Chile, and the Russian Federation: A Comparative Study

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kildeev, A. (2025). Legal Regulation of the Mining Industry in Peru, Chile, and the Russian Federation: A Comparative Study. Scientific Platform XXI Century, No. 8, November (2025), pp.16-31, www. episs.ru

detail.abstract: This paper is a published article. It originally appeared in Scientific Platform XXI Century, Issue 8, November (2025), pp. 16-31, www.episs.ru This article presents a comparative legal analysis of the mining regulatory frameworks of Peru, Chile, and the Russian Federation-three major resource-producing jurisdictions that represent distinct legal traditions and institutional models. Despite differences in constitutional structures and administrative practice, all three systems address similar core challenges: subsoil ownership, concession design, servitude rights, environmental obligations, investor protection, and the balance between state control and private participation. The study contrasts Peru's mixed concession-servitude regime (Ley 27651), Chile's constitutionally protected mining rights supported by strong judicial guarantees, and Russia's licensing model characterized by federal discretion and strategic-sector restrictions. Special attention is given to the mechanisms of granting mining rights, the distinction between exploration and exploitation stages, access to surface lands, and the scope of regulatory oversight. The article demonstrates that institutional clarity and regulatory predictability-rather than geological potential alone-determine investment attractiveness. Latin American systems provide comparatively transparent and stable frameworks, while the Russian model remains administratively rigid, limiting competitiveness despite vast mineral reserves. The study contributes to comparative mining law, natural-resource governance, and cross-jurisdictional regulatory design by offering an integrated analytical model for assessing mining regimes.

title: The Sovereign Data Axiom: A Protocol for Ending Contaminated Data in Human Research

detail.title: The Sovereign Data Axiom: A Protocol for Ending Contaminated Data in Human Research
detail.abstract: For decades, human-subjects research has been built on a fundamental error: the interpretation of non-response as data. We demonstrate that null behavioral results are scientifically uninterpretable, being indistinguishable from ego defense, emotional overload, or shame, thus rendering vast swathes of psychological, UX, and clinical findings invalid. This paper introduces the Sovereign Data Axiom, which states that only unprompted, sovereign behavioral change constitutes valid signal. From this, we derive a strict, six-step methodological protocol that replaces coercion with invitation and performance with truth. We conclude that the adoption of this protocol is necessary to end the era of contaminated data in human research.

title: The Ripple Effect: Nepal's 2015 Earthquake and Age at First Birth
affiliations: and University of Oklahoma

detail.title: The Ripple Effect: Nepal's 2015 Earthquake and Age at First Birth
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of Nepal's devastating 2015 earthquake with magnitude 7.8 on women's age at first birth (A1B), contributing to our understanding of how people change their reproductive decision in developing countries like Nepal. With a Difference in Difference design using pooled cross-sectional data from three rounds of Nepal Demographic and Health Surveys (2011, 2016, 2022), we compare the A1B of 14 severely affected districts against 61 unaffected districts before and after the earthquake. Our results show that women in earthquake-affected areas delayed their first birth by approximately 0.4-0.6 years (4.8-7.2 months) compared to women in unaffected districts. These effects persist for at least four years following the disaster. The impact varied significantly across population subgroups: older women, Muslims, and those with less education experienced the most pronounced delays. Mechanism analysis reveals that the earthquake increased the likelihood of mothers working in skilled manual labor by 2 percentage points (p < 0.01) and this was a key channel linking the earthquake exposure to delay in A1B.

title: Behavioral Measures of Economic Confidence and Their Relationship to Economic Output
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Behavioral Measures of Economic Confidence and Their Relationship to Economic Output
detail.abstract: Recognizing the distortions of self-assessed measures of confidence, such as the consumer confidence index, this paper looks towards behavioral measures of confidence, most notably, the propensity to spend. This is defined as the ratio of household final consumption to disposable resources. Using OECD, World Bank, and Federal Reserve economic data for 14 advanced countries with enough datapoints, this paper additionally shows that there is a strong correlation between the propensity to spend and GDP change (β≈ 0.0085, p<1x10-8) as well as its ∆ series (β≈0.0094, p<1x10-10). Supplementary measures that can be used for more countries show similar trends. This measurement reacts sharply during downturns such as 2008 and 2020, suggesting recessions may be confidence-driven. As this index, as well as the other indices, are derived from directly quantifiable data, they provide a transparent and internationally comparable alternative to self-assessed confidence metrics.

title: Analysis Of the Relationship Between Good Corporate Governance and Environmental Sustainability in Islamic Banking

detail.abstract: This research aims to examine how the application of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) principles such as transparency, accountability, and social responsibility can have an impact on environmental sustainability in Islamic banking operations. However, there are several challenges in its implementation, especially related to strengthening the transparency and independence of the Sharia Supervisory Board (DPS) in supervising sustainability aspects, as well as optimizing governance mechanisms so that they are not only formalistic but also substantive in strategic decision-making.

detail.abstract: Across scientific domains, "value" is defined inconsistently: engineers emphasize performance, economists emphasize utility, biologists emphasize fitness, computer scientists emphasize prediction accuracy, and organizational theorists emphasize coordination efficiency. Despite this fragmentation, all purposeful systems-biological, technological, organizational, and institutional-operate by reducing unnecessary dissipation relative to their functional roles. This paper proposes a unified structural definition of value: the reduction of avoidable waste relative to the system's purpose-function, boundary, and time horizon. Total waste decomposes into unavoidable waste (the physical and structural entropy floor) and avoidable waste (structural inefficiency). Across thermodynamics, cybernetics, evolutionary biology, economics, and artificial intelligence, all mechanisms of waste reduction fall into three independent generative levers: Sophistication (improved internal capability), Simplification (reduced friction or interaction complexity), and Scale (expanded functional organization across components or agents). The theory integrates two necessary constraints: the Boundary Validity Principle, preventing misattribution of waste displacement as value creation, and the Horizon-Setting Principle, ensuring proper classification of redundancy, slack, and resilience across time scales. A third constraint, the Horizon-Bounding Principle, limits possible horizons to the functional lifespan of the system and its enclosing environment. Three meta-level transformations-Optimization, Innovation, and Recontextualizationexplain incremental improvements, mechanistic revolutions, and major transitions in individuality or institutional form. The framework generates falsifiable predictions, aligns with empirical patterns across disciplines, and provides the foundations for formal proofs, computational implementations, and cross-domain systems analysis. This working paper presents the complete v2.2 framework, including appendices on taxonomy, formal axioms, mathematical structures, domain models, and computational implementations.

detail.title: Formal And Informal Writing Styles
detail.abstract: This paper examines the key differences between formal and informal writing styles, focusing on their purposes, linguistic features, and appropriate contexts of use. Formal writing is typically used in academic, professional, and official communication, characterized by precise vocabulary, complex sentence structures, objective tone, and adherence to grammatical conventions. In contrast, informal writing is commonly found in personal messages, casual conversations, and digital communication; it features colloquial expressions, contractions, simpler sentence patterns, and a more personal or conversational tone. Understanding the distinctions between these styles enables writers to communicate more effectively by selecting the register that aligns with their audience and communicative goals. The study highlights the importance of audience awareness, situational context, and communicative purpose in choosing between formal and informal writing.

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the integration of Sharia Good Corporate Governance (GCG) with the concept of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) in the latest Islamic finance industry, especially in Indonesia. The method used is a qualitative literature study by collecting and analyzing various journal articles, research reports, and the latest policy documentation in the last five years. The results of the study show that the integration of Sharia GCG and ESG is able to increase institutional compliance with Sharia principles while strengthening sustainability governance that focuses on environmental and social aspects. The implementation of this integration also has a positive impact on the performance of financial and non-financial institutions, especially through the development of green financial products and inclusive financing. However, there are challenges such as differences in standards and human resource capacity that need to be overcome. The implications of this research encourage regulators to strengthen sustainable policy frameworks that are in line with Sharia principles and invite Islamic financial institutions to adopt ESG reporting in a transparent manner and to systematically achieve inclusive and sustainable economic development.

title: DNA-Inspired Time Series Encoding: A Glimpse Into The Next 4-Hour Timeframe

detail.title: DNA-Inspired Time Series Encoding: A Glimpse Into The Next 4-Hour Timeframe
detail.abstract: In this work, we introduce a bio-inspired encoding framework for forecasting the direction of financial time series. Motivated by the limitations of linear models and the opacity of many deep learning approaches, we draw an analogy to genetics: observable micro-patterns are encoded into symbolic "Financial DNA" sequences. These sequences are then analyzed using a probabilistic state-transition mechanism to estimate the likelihood of subsequent market directions. We evaluate the approach on Bitcoin hourly OHLCV data with a rolling backtest. Among the horizons considered, modeling transitions from current Financial DNA patterns to the 4-hour-ahead price direction yields the strongest results, achieving a win ratio of 0.729. The findings suggest that compact, interpretable symbolic representations can capture salient, recurring structures in noisy, non-stationary markets and support effective directional forecasts.

detail.abstract: The Empty Brain Hypothesis (EBH) proposes a model-agnostic framework for identifying silent epistemic gaps in large language models (LLMs). EBH formalizes a tri-state cognitive architecture—Satiated, Empty, and Overfed—capturing how LLMs drift into hallucinations, representational collapse, and biased overfitting. The Empty Brain Model (EBM) introduces operational metrics including perplexity spikes, semantic drift, and the Bayesian-inspired Gap Score G(t)G(t)G(t). The framework develops bio-inspired “hunger signals” and feeding protocols enabling proactive epistemic regulation. Experiments on Llama-3 variants show up to 42% hallucination reduction and F1 = 0.66 gap detection performance. A multi-model case study with Grok, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, and NotebookLM reveals shared architectural voids. EBH reframes AI reliability as a problem of epistemic nourishment rather than data abundance.

title: Cognitive Fallow in AI Labour Markets: A Global Framework with an Australian Evidence Snapshot
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Cognitive Fallow in AI Labour Markets: A Global Framework with an Australian Evidence Snapshot
detail.abstract: This paper introduces cognitive fallow as a cohort level condition in which highly educated new entrants experience prolonged, involuntary under utilisation because artificial intelligence (AI) has automated or reallocated the entry level cognitive tasks that historically served as stepping stones into professional work. The concept is situated within task based technological change, graduate over education, and search and matching literatures. I formalise a simple mechanism in which AI reduces firms' incentives to post junior vacancies and raises experience thresholds, and propose a Cognitive Fallow Index (CFI) that can be implemented using standard labour market microdata. The CFI is defined as a composite of three components for exposed occupations: graduate underemployment, the median time to first relevant job, and the share of entry level postings in vacancy data. I distinguish between the full CFI, a data constrained CFI lite based on aggregate proxies, and a macro hazard based CFI L that uses cross country exit hazards from graduate unemployment to provide a simple comparative read on expected fallow durations. Empirically, I present two applications. First, an Australian snapshot for July 2025 shows that a national CFI lite constructed from the Internet Vacancy Index and Graduate Outcomes Survey does not signal a country wide cognitive fallow condition, which highlights how aggregation can mask field specific bottlenecks. Second, a macro hazard illustration for the United States, the European Union, China, and Australia demonstrates pronounced differences in expected fallow durations. The United States exhibits short spells while Australia records the longest. These cross country patterns underscore the importance of labour market slack and vacancy density, and show that AI readiness scores alone are not informative about entry level dynamics.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Bollinger Bands in cryptocurrency trading by contrasting two foundational interpretations: breakout (trend-following) and mean reversion (pullback) across multiple timeframes and market regimes using BTC/USDT data from July 2017 to March 2022. High-resolution backtesting reveals that Bollinger Bands exhibit regime dependent behavior, with each strategy's performance contingent on volatility structure and directional persistence. During the Bear Phase (2018), breakout strategies outperformed by aligning with volatility expansions, while mean-reversion signals failed amid sustained declines. In the Accumulation Phase (2018-2020), mean reversion regained limited profitability in calmer markets, though breakout setups maintained superior risk-adjusted returns. The Bull Run (2020-2021) represented the most favorable environment for both frameworks, breakout captured sustained momentum, whereas mean reversion achieved exceptional gains by exploiting shortterm corrections. Conversely, the Distribution Phase (2021-2022) showed the degradation of both approaches as trend conviction weakened. This research contributes to the literature on cryptocurrency market microstructure and algorithmic trading by: (1) reframing Bollinger Band analysis through a behavioral lens contrasting two core trading philosophies; (2) systematically evaluating their efficacy across timeframes and macro-market regimes; and (3) offering evidence-based insights into the contextual suitability of volatility-based indicators for high-noise, continuously traded markets.

detail.title: What is Budget and Why is it Important
detail.abstract: This article explores the What is the budget and why is it important? By searching data, how much important and impact to the society. After analyzing emphasize budget is prepare humans from rainy days or crisis in public. A budget is a plan for how you'll direct your income to cover your expenses, afford your wants and set aside money for the future. Not only can a budget help you stay afloat now, but it can help you build financial stability for the future. When you create a budget, you have the opportunity to get clear on where your money is going and look for areas you may want to change. Here are four reasons why you should budget. 1. Budgeting Helps You Avoid Overspending Without a budget, it can be easy to lose track of how much you're spending on what. Dining out, shopping online, going to events with friends-splurges big and small can add up to drain your bank account. With a budget, you can get a clear sense of how much you can afford to spend in the different areas of your life. After setting aside the funds needed to cover your housing payment and bills, you can allocate cash toward other essentials like food and toiletries. Then, you can determine how much you'll leave yourself for discretionary spending. By setting spending limits, you can avoid overdrawing your bank account or missing bill payments. 3. Budgeting Can Keep You out of Debt Impulse spending is a real risk when you have easy access to credit, and overspending on credit cards can leave you with a balance you can't pay off. But carrying a balance month to month can mean forking over money to high interest rates. Once you're in debt, it's easy to spiral deeper, and getting out can become challenging. By using a budget with your credit card, you can make sure it works for you rather than against you. And if you're already carrying credit card debt or high-interest loans, you can get back on track by creating a debt repayment plan and budget. Remember that paying more than the minimum on your debts can help you save substantial amounts of money on interest long term.

detail.title: Bridging the Student Loan Bankruptcy Gap

detail.abstract: In November 2022, the Department of Justice and Department of Education announced sweeping reforms designed to make student loan bankruptcy discharge more accessible to struggling borrowers. Drawing upon an original dataset of more than six hundred adversary proceedings filed during the first year of implementation, this article presents the first empirical analysis of whether these reforms have achieved their goal and bridged the “Student Loan Bankruptcy Gap”—the chasm between those who could benefit from bankruptcy discharge and those who actually pursue it. The results are mixed but suggest the gap, although narrowed, remains wide. On the positive side, success rates have reached 87% in the post-reform period. But on the negative side, filings remain remarkably low. This article evaluates the reforms along four key metrics of success and proposes solutions to make bankruptcy relief more accessible to struggling borrowers.

detail.abstract: Modern financial markets rely on frictions created by settlement delay, latency asymmetry, fragmented venues, and embedded credit windows. These frictions shape the behavior of market makers, internalizers, and high-frequency traders by pricing timing uncertainty and settlement risk into spreads and execution quality. Deterministic, interval-based settlement restructures this environment by ensuring that execution and completion occur within a single assured event. Principal risk declines, timing advantages contract, and credit no longer bridges incompatible settlement cycles. Liquidity becomes a network property accessed through global routing rather than a venue-specific inventory, and market mechanisms converge toward more stable and predictable designs. This paper examines how equity and multi-asset markets function when settlement friction approaches zero. Using deterministic settlement as a model architecture, the analysis draws on BIS Innovation Hub pilots and established microstructure theory to evaluate how execution, liquidity formation, collateral mobility, and systemic behavior change under synchronized finality. Deterministic settlement reorganizes rather than eliminates risk, creating a market structure in which liquidity and price formation operate within a unified and coordinated topology.

title: Transportation Construction and Regional Economic Growth: A Structural Model and its Empirical Analysis

detail.title: Transportation Construction and Regional Economic Growth: A Structural Model and its Empirical Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper develops a structural growth model to examine how transportation infrastructure investment affects regional economic performance in China, with a particular focus on differences between highly developed and less developed areas. Building on a modified Solow framework, I incorporate transportation capital as a separate production factor and derive an intensive-form equilibrium that highlights diminishing marginal returns and heterogeneous dynamic responses across regions. The empirical analysis uses data from 15 Chinese provinces and tests the model’s predictions by comparing transportation investment, transportation density, and per capita GDP across city and rural areas. The results show that increases in transportation density promote economic growth in rural regions but have limited or even negative effects in highly developed urban areas. These findings support the model’s prediction that transportation infrastructure yields large gains in underdeveloped regions that have not reached their steady-state infrastructure level, while its marginal impact declines sharply once a region becomes saturated. The study offers policy implications for China’s ongoing infrastructure-led development strategy, emphasizing the need for differentiated investment priorities based on regional development stages.

detail.abstract:
Climate risks are reshaping institutional and individual investment strategies, influencing market dynamics, and advancing sustainability initiatives. This paper delves into the pivotal influence of climate hazards on financial decision-making, elaborating on how investors identify, evaluate, and incorporate these risks into their investment tactics. It explores the developing approaches to risk assessment and their consequences for future market trends, supported by changes in regulations, enhancements in financial reporting, and findings from behavioral economics. This research specifically investigates the question: How does the Environmental component of ESG scores influence idiosyncratic risk in the health care providers and services, health care equipment and supplies, and household durables sectors? This analysis is guided by the following core hypotheses: Null Hypothesis (H0): The Environmental component of ESG scores does not significantly influence the idiosyncratic risk of firms in the health care providers and services, health care equipment and supplies, and household durables sectors. Alternative Hypothesis (H1): The Environmental component of ESG scores significantly influences the idiosyncratic risk of firms in these sectors.Literature suggests that environmental initiatives can cause idiosyncratic risk to both decrease and increase. Studies like El Ghoul et al. (2011) and Hoepner et al. (2019) demonstrate that strong environmental practices can reduce risk through improved demand stability and broader investor bases. 
Conversely,Becchetti et al. (2015) and Stellner et al. (2015) show that intensive environmental investments may elevate risk due to high upfront costs and rigid management structures. This mixed evidence highlights the necessity of empirical testing to clarify the relationship within these distinct industry sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of public-private partnerships in fostering robust financial markets and real-economy growth, using Silicon Valley in the United States and South Korea as case studies. It highlights how government initiatives-such as targeted research funding, infrastructure development, and policy support-combined with active venture capital and strong stock markets, have enabled companies like Apple, Alphabet, Samsung, Hyundai, and Kia to achieve global competitiveness. The analysis demonstrates that strategic state intervention does not replace private enterprise but complements it, creating conditions for innovation, investment, and long-term market sustainability. The findings underscore the importance of aligning public policy with financial-market mechanisms to enhance both economic growth and market efficiency.

title: State and Local Tax Policy in a Time of Telework

detail.title: State and Local Tax Policy in a Time of Telework
detail.abstract: State and local tax systems are constrained by the geographic location of individuals and economic activity. The rise of telework weakens this linkage by decoupling a worker's state of residence from the employer's location, creating new challenges for the design of personal income taxes, corporate income taxes, and unemployment insurance. Using Census data, we show that teleworkers are significantly more likely than non-teleworkers to relocate to lower-tax states and, through such migration, achieve significantly larger reductions in their state and local fiscal burden. Motivated by this evidence, we evaluate alternative principles for sourcing labor income for tax purposes to the place of residence, the place of work, or the place of the employer-highlighting the efficiency, equity, and administrative tradeoffs each entails. We further discuss how the rise of remote work fundamentally changes the state and local corporate income taxes, property taxes, and sales taxes and unemployment insurance. Taken together, our results suggest that telework is likely to reallocate state and local tax bases away from larger, more agglomerated jurisdictions toward smaller and more geographically remote ones, with important implications for subnational public finances.

detail.abstract: Pension funds have a pivotal role in financial systems, managing significant assets and contributing to economic growth through capital market investments. Identifying the key factors that influence their performance is essential for ensuring sustainable and adequate pension systems. The paper aims to identify the determinants of pension fund performance that directly contribute to competitiveness in financial markets by enabling efficient capital allocation and improved governance. The research employed two methods: a systematic literature review (SLR) and a bibliometric analysis (BA). The results indicate that five main factors influence pension fund performance: capital market developments, fund size and investment characteristics, corporate governance, behavioural and political influences, and regulatory and legislative environment. A bibliometric analysis reveals current trends in pension fund performance research and examines the relationship between the quality of a country's pension system and the origin of relevant research. The results provide valuable insights for fund managers, policymakers, and other stakeholders, thereby enhancing the decisionmaking process and deepening the understanding of the implications for pension fund performance, pension systems, and pension beneficiaries.

detail.abstract: We enhance the Universal Portfolio Shrinkage Approximator (UPSA) of Kelly et al. (2023) by making it more robust with respect to estimation noise and covariate shift. UPSA optimizes the realized Sharpe ratio using a relatively small calibration window, leveraging ridge penalties and cross-validation to yield better portfolios. Yet, it still suffers from the staggering amount of noise in financial data. We propose two methods to make UPSA more robust and improve its efficiency: time-averaging of the optimal penalty weights and using the Average Oracle correlation eigenvalues to make covariance matrices less noisy and more robust to covariate shift. Combining these two long-term averages outperforms UPSA by a large margin in most specifications.

Chapter 1 (Genesis) reframes origins: two primal leanings, Love (God) and the Hunger for More (the Adversary), precede a cosmos born in a great unfolding; humanity awakens in the cognitive revolution; the Old and New Testaments arise; and the author, Yosef of Nazareth, answers the Holy Spirit's call to inaugurate a testament that stays current through refinement. title: The Psychology Behind Market Doomscrolling: How Negative Financial News Shapes Risk Aversion in Young Investors

detail.title: The Psychology Behind Market Doomscrolling: How Negative Financial News Shapes Risk Aversion in Young Investors
detail.abstract: This study examines market doomscrolling, defined as the repetitive consumption of negatively valenced financial news and its causal effects on risk perceptions and portfolio choice among young, inexperienced investors (ages 16-24). Integrating psychological theory (negativity bias, availability heuristic, affect heuristic, loss aversion) with emerging empirical evidence on news sentiment and retail trading, I propose and implement a randomized online experiment comparing exposure to negative vs neutral/positive financial news feeds. The paper reports predicted effects, statistical analysis plans, robustness checks, mediation and moderation tests, and policy implications. Results are expected to show that short-term exposure to negative financial news increases perceived market risk and reduces allocations to risky assets, with stronger effects among individuals with a higher baseline doomscrolling tendency. Conflicting evidence and boundary conditions (contrarian retail flows, misinformation effects among confident investors) are discussed. The appendix contains full stimuli, survey items, and an analysis script outline.

title: Noisy Truth Beats Precise Lies: Blockchain-Enabled Information Equilibria
affiliations: Monash University, Tel Aviv University and Monash University

detail.title: Noisy Truth Beats Precise Lies: Blockchain-Enabled Information Equilibria
detail.abstract: Truth-telling is essential to efficient allocation of resources but is often undermined by strategic misreporting. We show how verifiably fair randomness, complemented by other blockchain functionalities, can lead to truth-telling at the cost of introduction of random noise in information transmission. The optimal trade-off between truthfulness and precision yields equilibria that outperform those attainable without randomization in information transmission. We characterize two classes of information equilibria: information designated to directly trigger value transfer via decentralized consensus ("enforcive information"), and strategic information sharing between Bayesian-rational decision makers ("advisive information"). Our findings demonstrate usefulness of randomized transmission in broad financial settings and illustrate the benefits of blockchain technology for optimal mechanism design.

detail.abstract: This paper has significantly reviewed how the Philippine educational system supports the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) strand, whether the system fully supports the international standards, and if it is capable of meeting the quality standards. Although the making of this curriculum, which stands for the spiral progression and inquiry-based learning, is theoretically harmonized with the international standards, its usability and practicality of using these are very weak. Emerging problems in the implementation occur in many schools, such as lack of resources in laboratories, lack of teachers' trainings, old-fashioned content of the curriculum, and access gaps, all of which prevent scientific learning. Moreover, the results in the PISA and TIMSS are very disappointing, showing an emerging disconnect between the promise in policy and the realities in the classroom setting. This continuously hinders the competitiveness of the nonintegration of modern skills or domains in this strand, such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and climate science. Having a true readiness in this STEM curriculum in the Philippines needs reform, by which this paper argues that it is a matter of investment in this country to make theoretical alignment into a future-ready system of STEM education.

detail.abstract: This MCM Manual offers basic advice on how to do multicriteria mapping (MCM). It suggests how to: go about designing and building a typical MCM project; engage with participants; analyse results; and get the most out of the online MCM tool. The online MCM software tool provides its own operational help. So this Manual is more focused on the general approach. There are no rigid rules. MCM is structured, but very flexible. It allows many more detailed features than can be covered here. MCM users are encouraged to think for themselves and be responsible and creative. But there are some key underlying MCM values. The most crucial are as follows: 1) Inclusion: MCM aims to promote more inclusive, equitable and accessible appraisal. This means engaging in a respectful and balanced way, with a diversity of relevant perspectives – especially those most often marginalized. 2) Opening Up: MCM aims to help ‘open up’ appraisal. This means giving balanced attention to exploring and illuminating contending views. Using MCM just to aggregate a single final view has the effect instead of ‘closing down’. 3) Agency: MCM aims to ‘put participants in the driving seat’. An MCM project should be designed, implemented and analysed to maximise the agency of participants over the ways in which their own perspectives are represented. 4) Transparency: MCM only ‘opens up’, if results are conveyed fully and clearly to all parties with an interest in debates over the focal goal. Depending on context, this means publishing results and giving reasonable access to data. This Manual gives advice on how these values can best be realised in practice.

This study looks at how Spain's agricultural output, export results, and long-term economic prospects have been impacted by climate change. It also examines the development of Spain's energy and climate policies, emphasizing the nation's early adoption of renewable energy sources and its initiatives to lower greenhouse gas emissions.

The paper examines the growth of solar, wind, and green hydrogen projects and their effects on jobs, energy security, and sustainable growth based on indicators and policy developments. The results indicate that although Spain has made great strides in the use of clean energy, more work is required to improve resilience to mounting climate pressures, speed up emissions reduction, and fortify adaptation.

detail.title: Salience Theory of Belief Updating and Expectation Formation
detail.abstract: We present a salience theory of belief updating and expectation formation, integrating the concept of salience with the learning dynamics of the Kalman filter to formalize how decision makers selectively focus their attention on, and overreact to, salient surprises. This model incorporates key properties of salience theory-boundedness, ordering, uncertainty, threshold, and asymmetry-and exhibits relevance effect, asymmetric surprise sensitivity and probability weighting. Our framework provides new insights into context-dependent behavioral phenomena including the "first-time effect," the pleasure paradox, overreaction to disconfirming and expected information, attribution bias, projection bias, inattention to shrouded attributes, overreaction to a series of news and extreme outliers, and the endowment and personal experience effects.

detail.title: The Sentiment Channel of Fiscal Policy ‡
detail.abstract: How does government spending stimulate the economy? We uncover a new transmission channel-the sentiment channel-by showing that government spending makes firms overoptimistic about their future demand, thereby stimulating investment and output. We assemble a novel dataset linking microdata on Italian firms' sales, sales forecasts, and public procurement contracts. Using a natural experiment that shifted public spending across municipalities, we find that an increase in government demand makes firms systematically overoptimistic about their future sales. This overoptimism is pervasive, as firms also raise their expectations about export sales. To interpret these findings, we develop a theory of expectations in which shocks to total sales make a firm overoptimistic about both its public and private sales. We embed this model of expectations in a heterogeneous-firm New Keynesian model disciplined with our causal estimates. Government spending boosts firms optimism which prompts them to invest, crowding-in investment in general equilibrium-thereby doubling the government spending multiplier. This amplification is state-dependent: our model predicts that the multiplier is a third smaller during financial crises than in recessions without financial distress.
